## ADR-051: Middleware Request Logs (MID-10/11, MUI-9) — HTTP-client-event hook, redact-then-queue write path, and split retention

**Status:** Accepted (design) — 2026-08-28 (grilled via `/mattpocock-skills:grilling`, four rounds, before any code touched)

**Context:** `docs/prd.md` §15's 2026-08-28 reconciliation pass on the Middleware Panel row confirmed MID-10/11 (backend) and MUI-9 (admin UI) as the one genuinely unbuilt piece of that row — no `request_log`-equivalent table or model exists anywhere in the codebase (confirmed via grep), and `docs/foundation-security.md` §7 already carries an explicit, still-unchecked line naming exactly this feature: *"Request logs redact credentials and excess PII before being written (MID-10)"* — a standing requirement, not a new invention of this ADR.

Investigation before grilling found the real shape of the problem: `SupplierAdapter` (`app/Services/Supplier/SupplierAdapter.php`) has 5 methods (`checkBalance`, `listProducts`, `createOrder`, `checkStatus`, `validatePlayer`), and both real implementations (`GamevionAdapter`, `DigiflazzAdapter`) each build their own `Http::baseUrl()` client and call `->post()` independently at each method — there is no single existing choke point. `CircuitBreakingSupplierAdapter`'s `guarded()` helper wraps 4 of the 5 methods (not `validatePlayer`) but only sees the normalized `SupplierResponse`, not the raw HTTP request/response. Zero existing logging (`Log::` calls) exists in either adapter or the circuit breaker today. `player_validations` (ADR-021's 7-day-retained PII table) stores only the validation *outcome* (status/nickname/country/provider), not the raw call — no overlap with what this feature adds. `price_sync_runs`/`deactivation_logs` are per-sync-*run* granularity, not per-HTTP-*call* — also no overlap.

**Decision:**

1. **Scope: supplier-adapter calls only** — all 5 `SupplierAdapter` methods, for any adapter (today Gamevion/Digiflazz, automatically any future one). Payment gateway webhooks (Xendit/CHIP) are explicitly **out of scope** — a separate future item under §6.23 Payment & Webhook Integrity, not folded in here.
2. **Hook mechanism: Laravel's HTTP client `RequestSending`/`ResponseReceived` events, listened to globally** — not a new decorator, not per-adapter logging code. This touches neither the `SupplierAdapter` interface nor its implementations' method bodies (matches this project's "deep modules, stable seams" convention), and automatically covers `validatePlayer` too, which the existing circuit-breaker decorator doesn't wrap. Each adapter call site gains a small context tag (`supplier_id`, `call_type`, `order_id` where applicable) passed via HTTP client request options, so the generic event has enough to attribute a row without redesigning `SupplierResponse`.
3. **Circuit-breaker preemptive skips get a synthetic log row too** (`outcome = skipped_breaker_open`), distinct from a real HTTP failure — `guarded()` short-circuits before any request is sent, and losing that distinction would make the log unable to answer "did the supplier actually fail, or did we never even ask." ~~Same signal MUI-1's still-ungrilled Dashboard would eventually want to show.~~ **MUI-1 built 2026-08-28 — see [ADR-052](./adr.md)** — deliberately scoped thinner than this: a "recent calls" feed reusing `listRequestLogs()` as-is, not a dedicated breaker-skip-rate view.
4. **Write path is redact-then-queue-then-write, never inline-then-redact.** The event listener classifies and strips secret-tagged payload keys *before* the row ever reaches the queue or the database — directly implementing `foundation-security.md` §7's "redact... before being written" line, not a lesser after-the-fact scrub. The actual insert is dispatched as a queued job (Redis/Horizon, `ADR-048`), not written inline, so the one customer-facing synchronous call in this set (`validatePlayer`) never gets slower because of logging.
5. **Payload depth: full request+response body by default**, masked. This is the feature's real debugging value — a metadata-only log (status code, duration, nothing else) would not have surfaced the real `callback_url`-missing production bug (`ADR-006`'s 2026-07-29 addendum). One deliberate exception: `listProducts`' response (a full supplier catalog dump) is truncated to an item count + small sample, not stored in full — repetitive, large, and already covered at the right granularity by `price_sync_runs`/`deactivation_logs`.
6. **Rows from `createOrder`/`checkStatus` carry a nullable `order_id` FK** — cheap column, lets a future Order Detail view filter "every supplier call for this order" directly; same FK-to-originating-entity convention `deactivation_logs` already uses toward `price_sync_run_id`.
7. **Retention: 30-day default pruning, except `validatePlayer` rows follow `player_validations`' existing 7-day PII window (`ADR-021`)** rather than the blanket 30 — those rows carry the same player-account nickname/ID category that window already governs, and a debug log copy of PII shouldn't outlive the record the PII-retention decision was actually made for. A new pruning command mirrors `PrunePlayerValidationsCommand`'s shape rather than extending it (different table, different owning concern).
8. **Table name: `supplier_request_logs`**, not the more generic `request_logs` the PRD's own MID-10/11 wording might suggest — decision 1 already scopes this to supplier-adapter calls only, and a generic name would collide with (or force a rename around) a future payment-webhook logging table under §6.23.
9. **UI: standalone `/middleware/request-logs` screen (MUI-9)**, not folded into `/middleware/suppliers` or `/middleware/sandbox` — list + filter (supplier/call_type/outcome/date range) + a detail modal showing the (already-redacted) raw payload, same interaction shape as Price Sync's own Sync Details modal.
10. ~~**Forward reference, not a commitment:** this ADR notes `supplier_request_logs` as the eventual data source for MUI-1's still-ungrilled unified Dashboard (supplier cards, circuit-breaker state, a recent-API-call feed) — the same anticipatory note `ADR-019` left via `CircuitBreaker::state()` ahead of `DASH`'s own dashboard screen being built.~~ **Fulfilled 2026-08-28 — see [ADR-052](./adr.md).** MUI-1's landing page reads `supplier_request_logs` via `listRequestLogs()` exactly as anticipated here, alongside `getDashboardHealth()` (the same `CircuitBreaker::state()`-backed endpoint `ADR-019`'s own anticipatory note pointed at) for supplier cards/circuit state.

**Rationale:** Decision 2 is the load-bearing architectural call this ADR exists to record — a global HTTP-client-event listener achieves full coverage across all 5 methods (including the one the existing circuit-breaker decorator doesn't wrap) without reshaping the `SupplierAdapter` seam or touching either real adapter's method bodies. Decisions 4/5/7 together directly close the standing, previously-unchecked `foundation-security.md` §7 requirement rather than leaving it open through this build too. Decision 8 keeps the table's scope as precise as decision 1's own scope boundary, so a future webhook-logging feature never has to contend with (or rename around) this one.

**Consequence to track:** the secret-field classification this feature's redaction step relies on should reuse/extend the shared field-shape schema (see build addendum — `SupplierConfigSchema`) rather than invent a second classification scheme — if a new supplier adds a new secret-shaped config field, both places need to move together or redaction silently misses it. If a future payment-webhook request-logging feature gets built under §6.23, it gets its own table, never squeezed into `supplier_request_logs` (decision 8's boundary). ~~If MUI-1's Dashboard is eventually grilled and built, it should read `supplier_request_logs`, not stand up a second, parallel write path.~~ **Fulfilled 2026-08-28 — see [ADR-052](./adr.md)**, exactly as anticipated: no second write path was ever created.

**Build addendum, 2026-08-28 (same day) — shipped on `feature/adr-051-request-logs`, stacked on `fix/supplier-config-guard`.** All 10 decisions shipped; one implementation-level correction to decision 2, found while building, not a re-litigation of the decision's intent:

- **Decision 2 correction:** Laravel's `RequestSending`/`ResponseReceived` HTTP client events, as literally named in the decision text, turned out to carry only the PSR-7 request/response — no way to attach a call's business context (supplier slug/call_type/order_id), since Guzzle-level request *options* (where that context would ride) never make it onto the event's `Request` object. Used Guzzle's per-request `on_stats` option instead (`SupplierRequestLogger::attach()`) — set locally inside each adapter's `client()` builder, so the callback closes over the context directly. Achieves the same intent decision 2 actually asked for (no `SupplierAdapter` interface change, no decorator, automatic coverage of `validatePlayer` too) — same "generic client-level hook, not per-call-site logging code" shape, just a different Laravel/Guzzle primitive than the one named. `client()` methods on both adapters gained `string $callType`/`?int $orderId` parameters to supply that context; `SupplierOrderRequest`/`SupplierStatusCheckRequest` gained an `orderId` field (decision 6), populated at their two real construction sites (`OrderFulfillmentService`, `CheckSupplierDeliveryJob`).
- **`SupplierController::FIELD_DEFINITIONS`** (private, decision 8/redaction's stated reuse target) was extracted to a new shared `App\Services\Supplier\SupplierConfigSchema` on the prerequisite `fix/supplier-config-guard` branch this one stacks on — both `SupplierController` (masking/`visibleConfig()`) and this feature's `SupplierRequestPayloadRedactor` (body-key redaction) now read the same source, closing the exact drift risk this ADR's own Consequence section flagged before it could ever open.
- **Redaction, concretely:** `SupplierRequestPayloadRedactor` always strips `Authorization`/`X-API-KEY` headers case-insensitively (covers Gamevion's header-based auth), plus any body key `SupplierConfigSchema` marks `secret` for that slug, plus one extra per-slug list (`digiflazz.sign` — an MD5 derived from the api_key, not the raw secret, but replayable for that exact call so redacted with the same discipline). Digiflazz's auth lives entirely in the body (no secret headers), Gamevion's entirely in headers (no secret body keys) — both paths are real, not hypothetical, and both are covered.
- **Circuit-breaker skip logging (decision 3):** `CircuitBreaker` gained a `name()` getter (its constructor name already *is* the supplier slug every binding constructs it with); `CircuitBreakingSupplierAdapter::guarded()` takes a `$callType` (+ `$orderId` for the two order-related methods) and dispatches `LogSupplierRequestJob` directly with `outcome=skipped_breaker_open` on an open breaker — bypassing `SupplierRequestLogger` entirely since there's no real HTTP transfer to hook `on_stats` onto.
- **`listProducts` truncation (decision 5):** response sampled to `item_count`/`sample` (first 3 items)/`truncated` when the decoded body's `data` key holds a list; falls back to storing the (redacted) body as-is for any non-list shape rather than guessing.
- **Real gap found and fixed before this was considered done, not shipped silently:** Horizon's supervisors (`config/horizon.php`) explicitly list which queue each one processes (`supervisor-orders` → `orders`, etc.) — the new `LogSupplierRequestJob`'s `supplier-request-logs` queue had no supervisor at all, so every dispatched job would have sat forever unprocessed with zero error, discovered only by trying to verify a real log row appear in the UI (a `php artisan queue:work redis --queue=supplier-request-logs --stop-when-empty` foreground drain proved the write path worked before Horizon itself was restarted). Fixed with a new `supervisor-supplier-request-logs` (mirrors `supervisor-backups`' shape, `tries=1`) in both `defaults` and every `environments` entry, plus a `waits` threshold — this is a real, generalizable lesson: **a new queue name needs a Horizon supervisor entry, not just `ShouldQueue` on the job,** the same way a new migration needs a local `php artisan migrate` (AGENTS.md's own second gotcha) — nothing enforces this at write time, it only surfaces as a silently-stuck queue.
- **Second real bug, found live in the same verification pass:** the Request Logs detail modal's "View" button initially passed the `DataTable` row template's own `item` object straight into dialog state (`setDetailLog(row)`, mirroring `BackupsPage`'s working `setConfirmDeleteRun(run)` pattern) — every field came back `undefined` in the dialog despite the same row rendering correctly in the table one line above. Root cause not fully isolated (suspected PrimeReact `DataTable` row-template object not being safe to hold past its own render cycle for a *nested* field like `supplier`, where `BackupRun`'s equivalent case never nests). Fixed by having "View" call `GET /api/middleware/request-logs/{id}` (`RequestLogController::show()`, already built for decision 9) instead of reusing the table's own object — also the more correct design regardless, since it's the canonical single-row fetch rather than trusting whatever the last list response happened to include.
- Test-suite discipline: `GamevionAdapterTest`/`DigiflazzAdapterTest`/`CircuitBreakingSupplierAdapterTest` are deliberately DB-free unit tests (no `RefreshDatabase`) — `LogSupplierRequestJob implements ShouldQueue`, and the test environment's `QUEUE_CONNECTION=sync` (`phpunit.xml`) executes a queued job inline the instant it's dispatched, which broke all three suites the moment adapters started dispatching it (`no such table: suppliers`). Fixed with `Queue::fake()` in each suite's `setUp()` — keeps their DB-free scope intact while still letting new tests assert *that* the right job was pushed with the right shape (`Queue::assertPushed(...)`).
- 17 new backend tests (`SupplierRequestPayloadRedactorTest`, `LogSupplierRequestJobTest`, `RequestLogControllerTest`, `PruneSupplierRequestLogsCommandTest`, plus new cases in the three adapter-level suites above); full backend suite **948/948 green**. `npx tsc --noEmit`/`eslint`/`next build` clean on `admin/`. Browser-verified live end-to-end (not just typechecked): a real `Refresh Balance` click against the real local Gamevion connection → `on_stats` → redacted → queued → drained via `queue:work --once` → row appears in `/middleware/request-logs` → detail modal shows `Authorization`/`X-API-KEY` correctly redacted and the real (unredacted, non-secret) response body.

**Consequence to track:** any future money-panel on this project that shows a "Revenue − Costs = Profit"-shaped breakdown should default to asking which population question 2 asked here — does the reconciliation need to hold, and if so, every line must share one scope — before writing the query, not after a founder notices the numbers don't add up. The Order History table's `—`-for-undelivered convention (decision 5) is new precedent; a future per-order profit display elsewhere should match it rather than inventing a third convention (`RM 0.00` vs. `—` vs. omitting the column).

## ADR-052: Middleware Panel closure batch — MUI-7 merged into Validators, MUI-1 as a thin `/middleware` landing page, MUI-4 dropped

**Status:** Accepted (design) — 2026-08-28 (grilled via `/mattpocock-skills:grilling`, four rounds, before any code touched)

**Context:** `docs/prd.md` §15's Middleware Panel row listed three remaining real gaps after ADR-051 (Request Logs) closed MID-10/11/MUI-9: **MUI-7** (standalone Validate Player tool), **MUI-4** (Games full catalog+export inside `/middleware`), and **MUI-1** (unified Dashboard: supplier cards, quick actions, recent API calls, circuit-breaker state). The founder no longer clearly remembered why these three were originally scoped as separate screens and asked for a genuine build-or-drop grilling rather than taking the backlog wording at face value.

Investigation before grilling found each item already overlaps existing, shipped screens:
- **MUI-7** ("Validate Player: game selector, player ID input, validation result, 'not supported for this game' state") overlaps the per-validator raw connectivity test already on `/middleware/validators` (MUI-5) — but that test calls `PlayerValidatorRegistry::resolve($key)->validate()` directly, bypassing the game→region-mapping resolution a real customer's checkout hits. The real customer-facing logic already exists and is already called from two other places: `storefront/src/lib/checkout.ts` (the wizard) and `admin/src/lib/orders.ts`'s `validatePlayerForResend()` (ORD-7 resend flow) — both hit the same public, no-auth `POST /api/games/{game}/validate-player` (`PlayerValidationController::store`).
- **MUI-4** ("Games: full game catalog with edit and export") overlaps `/admin/games` (catalog+edit, GAME-1..5/7, already built) and `/middleware/product-manager` (raw supplier catalog staging/promote flow) — no concrete export use-case (accounting, handoff, audit) was ever recorded, and reproducing an entire catalog+edit screen a second time inside `/middleware` just to add an unspecified export button has no clear justification.
- **MUI-1** ("Dashboard: supplier status cards, quick actions, recent API calls, circuit-breaker state") overlaps `DashboardService::health()` (ADR-045's Admin Dashboard System Health section — already renders per-supplier `name`/`balance`/`circuit_state` from `CircuitBreaker::state()`), `/middleware/request-logs` (ADR-051 — the "recent API calls" feed), and `/middleware/suppliers` (ADR-046 — the "quick actions": refresh balance, activate/deactivate). ADR-051 decision 10 had already flagged `supplier_request_logs` as MUI-1's anticipated future data source. `admin/src/app/middleware/page.tsx` itself already existed as a stale placeholder (`TODO: MUI-1 ... Placeholder until the Adapter layer exists` — the Adapter layer has been built since ADR-006).

**Decision:**

1. **MUI-7: merged onto `/middleware/validators`, not a standalone screen.** A new "Validate Player (by Game)" panel (`ValidateByGamePanel.tsx`) sits below the existing Validators list, reusing `validatePlayerForResend()` (widened to surface `country_code`/`redirect_game`, both already returned by the backend but previously untyped on this narrower caller) — zero new backend. The founder accepted the one real side-effect this reuse carries: `PlayerValidationController::store` writes a real `player_validations` row on every call, and `CheckoutController::assertPlayerIdIsValidated()` gates checkout purely on `game_id`+`player_id`+`server_id`+`status=valid` within a rolling window (default 30 min) — **not** session-bound (a deliberate, already-accepted design per the 2026-07-27 audit). An admin's test call therefore pre-clears checkout for that exact combo for the window, identical in kind to what any guest calling the same public endpoint could already do — not a new attack surface, so no `is_admin_test` flag or separate non-persisting endpoint was built for it.
2. **MUI-4: dropped entirely.** No screen, no export button, anywhere. `/admin/games` and `/middleware/product-manager` already cover the real workflow (promote → manage); no concrete demand for a duplicate view or an export was ever established.
3. **MUI-1: built as a thin, manual-refresh landing page at `/middleware`** (replacing the stale placeholder), not a new data source:
   - Suppliers section: reuses `getDashboardHealth()` (the exact endpoint Admin Dashboard's System Health already calls), rendering only `suppliers` (name/balance/circuit_state) — `stuck_orders`/`pending_payments` are intentionally omitted as out of this screen's scope.
   - Quick actions: a single "Manage Suppliers →" link to `/middleware/suppliers`, no inline mutation — action logic stays owned by that one screen.
   - Recent API calls: last 5 rows from `listRequestLogs(token, { per_page: 5 })` (the `RequestLogFilters` type gained an optional `per_page`, mirroring a parameter the backend controller already accepted but the admin client never declared) + a "View all →" link to `/middleware/request-logs`.
   - Manual "Refresh" button, no auto-poll — this is a glance-and-leave page, not a monitoring surface someone sits on the way Admin Dashboard's own 60s-polling System Health is.
   - No shared component extracted with Admin Dashboard's System Health section — the two screens' scopes differ (order-metrics vs. supplier-only) and the founder agreed sharing would be premature abstraction for a two-consumer, small-each case.

**Rationale:** Decision 1 is the load-bearing call — it gets MUI-7's real requirement (simulate what a customer actually experiences, not just poke a validator's provider) without adding a second screen or any backend, by recognizing the exact resolution logic already exists and is already called from two other places in the codebase. Decision 2 avoids building a screen and a feature (export) that nothing in the system or the founder's own memory could justify — the honest answer to "what's this for" was "not sure," which is a drop, not a build. Decision 3 keeps MUI-1 to what's actually missing (a `/middleware`-scoped at-a-glance view) rather than re-deriving data three other screens already serve correctly.

**Consequence to track:** if a future feature needs `player_validations` rows to exclude admin-originated test calls (e.g., a fraud/analytics feature starts reading that table), decision 1's accepted side-effect should be revisited then, not preemptively engineered around now. If MUI-1's landing page later grows real scope-specific data needs beyond the three reused sources, evaluate a dedicated backend view at that point rather than stretching `DashboardService::health()` to serve two different screens' evolving needs.

## ADR-053: Reviews (REV-1..5) — guest, order-linked submission via a real-time delivery-status trigger, admin-only moderation

**Status:** Accepted (design) — 2026-08-28 (grilled via `/mattpocock-skills:grilling`, three rounds, before any code touched)

**Context:** `docs/prd.md` §6.13/§15 REV-1..5 is a completely unbuilt feature (⬜/⬜, "Not blocked on supplier") — no `Review` model, migration, or route exists anywhere (confirmed via grep). Picked as the next backlog item once the Middleware Panel batch (ADR-052) closed. The spec itself only covers the admin moderation side (stats, table, approve/reject, bulk-approve-all, filters) — it says nothing about how a review actually gets created, which is the real load-bearing gap: the storefront is guest-checkout only (ADR-011, no customer accounts), so a review can't hang off a `User` the way a typical review system would.

Investigation before grilling found the shape already mostly dictated by existing code:
- `Order` has a single `package_id`/`game_id` (`belongsTo`, no multi-item cart) — a `Review` can key directly to `order_id` with no line-item complexity.
- No cash-refund path exists anywhere (ADR-004) — an order past `Delivered` never reverts, so there's no "review on a voided order" case to design around.
- `TrackOrderController` already establishes the guest-identity pattern this system uses: possessing the `order_number` (a ULID, ~80 bits of entropy) is the proof of ownership, no email pairing, no login. A review-submission endpoint should follow the identical pattern, not invent a new one.
- `storefront/src/components/order/OrderStatusTracker.tsx` (ADR-047) already unifies two update sources — a Reverb push on the public `order.{order_number}` channel and a 20s poll fallback — into one `order` state object, and already computes `delivery_status === "delivered"` as a terminal condition. This is the natural, already-existing hook point for a review prompt: no new real-time plumbing needed.
- `storefront/src/lib/placeholder-data.ts`'s `TestimonialsSection` is deliberately static/fake ("honest static content, not a fake dynamic system," same reasoning as Promotions) — a pre-existing, separate concern from this feature, not something this ADR touches.

**Decision:**

1. **Submission is guest, order-linked, gated on `delivery_status=Delivered`.** A review can only be submitted once an order has actually been delivered (not merely paid) — the customer must have received the product before rating it. Identity proof is the `order_number` alone, mirroring `TrackOrderController`'s existing pattern; no new auth/verification mechanism.
2. **One review per order.** `Review.order_id` is unique — a second submission attempt against an already-reviewed order is rejected, not silently overwritten or duplicated. This is the primary spam control; combined with the `order_number`'s own ~80-bit entropy, a plain `throttle:10,1` (matching `POST /api/checkout`'s own convention) is sufficient on the submission endpoint — no CAPTCHA or blacklist integration.
3. **Trigger UI: a popup modal, not an inline card, driven by a single derived condition — `order.delivery_status === 'delivered' && !order.has_review`.** Lives inside the existing `OrderStatusTracker.tsx` (shared by both `/order/status/[orderNumber]` and `/track-order`, per this codebase's existing "one component, two entry points" precedent) — fires identically whether the transition arrives live (Reverb push) or the page loads directly into an already-delivered order (initial poll), since both paths write into the same `order` state already. `TrackedOrder` (and `OrderStatusUpdated`'s broadcast payload) gains a new `has_review: boolean` field to drive this.
4. **No client-side dismiss-forever state.** Closing the modal without submitting does not set a cookie/`localStorage` flag — the modal reappears on any later visit to either entry point (same order_number) as long as `has_review` is still `false`. This is deliberately server-truth-only: once a real review lands, `has_review` flips server-side and the modal never shows again for that order, from any device/browser — no client state to keep in sync.
5. **Data model: `Review` reads `game`/`package` live via its `Order` relation, never duplicates/snapshots those columns.** `rating` (1-5, required), `comment` (nullable — REV-5's "with comment only" filter presumes some reviews have none), `status` (`pending` default / `approved` / `rejected`).
6. **No public display anywhere.** Approved reviews stay purely an internal admin moderation view, matching REV-1..5's own literal spec (which never mentions public display) — `TestimonialsSection`'s static content is untouched, a deliberately separate concern. Extending to a public/Testimonials-replacing display is left to a future, dedicated ADR once real review volume exists to justify the design work, not bundled in here.
7. **`average_rating` (REV-1's stat) is scoped to `status=approved` only** — a rejected/spam review shouldn't skew the one quality signal this admin-only feature produces.

**Rationale:** Decision 3 is the load-bearing call — it gets a real-time, no-nag-when-already-reviewed prompt essentially for free by recognizing `OrderStatusTracker.tsx` already unifies both delivery-status update sources into one piece of state, rather than building new polling/broadcast plumbing specific to this feature. Decision 4 keeps the "have they reviewed yet" question server-authoritative rather than device-local, which is both simpler (no client storage to manage) and more correct (a customer who dismisses on their phone and later opens `/track-order` on a laptop still gets prompted exactly once more, until they actually submit). Decision 6 keeps this ADR's scope to what REV-1..5 literally asks for — bundling a public-display redesign in here would conflate two separately-sized decisions.

**Consequence to track:** if a future ADR adds public display (decision 6's deferred branch), it needs its own scoping pass on which reviews are eligible (approved-only is the obvious default, consistent with decision 7) and whether it replaces or supplements `TestimonialsSection`. If `Order` ever gains real multi-item/line-item support, decision 1's "Review keys to Order directly" assumption should be revisited then, not before.

## ADR-054: Developer raw API tester (DEV-1/2, MUI-11) — typed-DTO editor over the real adapter seam, backend-driven dry-run, production-mode block on `createOrder`

**Status:** Accepted (design) — 2026-08-28 (grilled via `/mattpocock-skills:grilling`, two rounds, before any code touched)

**Context:** `docs/prd.md` §15 flagged this as the one remaining real gap in the Middleware Panel row (line 1421's own note: "deliberately not bundled into ADR-052's batch — different risk profile: fires raw requests at a live supplier API, needs its own grilling on sandbox-only enforcement / production-mode blocking / its own audit trail"). §6.18/§6.20 spec it thin: DEV-1 says "supplier API tester: check balance, test validate player, test create order with dry-run toggle"; DEV-2 says "raw JSON editor and response viewer, with credentials always masked." MUI-11 is the identical screen — one build satisfies both.

Investigation before grilling found the supporting infrastructure already exists, which shaped every decision below:
- `SupplierAdapter` (`app/Services/Supplier/SupplierAdapter.php`) exposes 5 methods, not the 3 the spec names: `checkBalance()`, `listProducts()`, `createOrder(SupplierOrderRequest)`, `checkStatus(SupplierStatusCheckRequest)`, `validatePlayer(string, ?string)`.
- Credential masking already has a single source of truth: `SupplierConfigSchema::fieldsFor($slug)` classifies each `api_config` key as `text`/`secret`/`boolean`, and `SupplierRequestPayloadRedactor` (ADR-051 decision 4) uses that same classification to redact both headers (`Authorization`, `X-Api-Key`) and body secrets before a request/response payload is ever persisted or displayed.
- Every real adapter call already flows through `SupplierRequestLogger::attach()` (ADR-051) via each adapter's shared `client()` — any call made through the real adapter is automatically logged to `supplier_request_logs`, no new logging path needed.
- Each adapter's credentials are bound server-side from `Supplier.api_config` (encrypted at rest, `hidden` on the model) at container-resolution time — no interface method takes credentials as a parameter, so a caller of `SupplierAdapter` can never see or pass a secret through it regardless of what this feature builds.
- [[feedback_sandbox_flag_leaks_into_health_checks]] (found live during ADR-046): each adapter's own sandbox/testing `api_config` flag behaves inconsistently — `GamevionAdapter`'s `sandbox` flag is a blanket header on every call via its shared `client()`; `DigiflazzAdapter`'s `testing` flag only affects its transaction-submission endpoint, confirmed **not** applied to `checkBalance()`. This is adapter-specific, not a platform-wide guarantee.
- This feature is orthogonal to the existing Sandbox Test Orders screen (`/middleware/sandbox`, ADR-018): that screen tests *this platform's own* order-lifecycle logic against a `FakeSupplierAdapter` that never makes a real network call and always writes a real `Order` row (`is_test=true`). This feature tests *the real supplier integration itself* — real adapters, real (or the supplier's own sandbox) network calls, no `Order` row ever created.

**Decision:**

1. **Expose all 5 `SupplierAdapter` methods**, not just the 3 named in DEV-1's spec text — `listProducts`/`checkStatus` are strictly lower-risk (read-only) than `createOrder`, and a developer tester covering a subset of the actual interface contract would be a worse tool for no safety gain.
2. **The JSON editor edits a typed DTO's fields, never a raw HTTP body sent straight to the supplier.** A `createOrder` test still goes through `SupplierOrderRequest` and the real `GamevionAdapter`/`DigiflazzAdapter::createOrder()` method — the editor changes what populates that DTO, not the wire format underneath it. This keeps `SupplierAdapter` as the stable seam AGENTS.md calls out (extend/use an implementation behind it, don't reshape or bypass it) and guarantees a value that was never validated by anything can't reach a live supplier's API as a raw body.
3. **Dry-run (default ON) means no network call at all** — the backend builds the exact same typed request object the real call would use and returns it as a preview; turning dry-run OFF is what actually dispatches the request through the real adapter. This is evaluated on the backend (not previewed client-side), so the preview is provably the same construction path a real send would use, not a JS approximation of it.
4. **`createOrder` is hard-blocked (not just confirm-dialoged) when dry-run is OFF and the target supplier's own sandbox/testing `api_config` flag is `false`.** The other 4 methods are read-only/side-effect-free from this platform's perspective and may live-fire regardless of the supplier's mode. `createOrder` is the one call with a real financial/order side-effect on the supplier's side, and per decision setup this screen has no `Order` row of its own to reconcile against if a real production order actually gets created by a test — so it's blocked outright rather than trusted to a warning dialog.
5. **`createOrder` test requests get a non-editable, prefixed reference (`DEVTEST-...`)**, never an admin-typed value — keeps this feature's calls unambiguously identifiable on the supplier's own side and structurally incapable of colliding with the real `reference_number` sequence real orders use.
6. **`checkStatus` accepts any admin-typed reference, including a real customer order's** — it's a pure read-only lookup against the supplier directly, useful for support/debugging without going through `/admin/orders`' own detail view.
7. **Real (non-dry-run) calls reuse `SupplierRequestLogger`/`supplier_request_logs` unchanged**, tagged with a `call_type` prefix (e.g. `dev_test_checkBalance`) so they're visibly distinguishable from order-flow-originated calls in the existing `/middleware/request-logs` viewer. No new log table. Dry-run previews are not logged — no network call occurred to log.
8. **The response viewer applies `SupplierRequestPayloadRedactor` to on-screen output**, not only to what gets persisted — a live response containing a secret-derived value (e.g. Digiflazz's `sign`) is masked the same way whether it's being written to a log row or shown directly to the admin who just triggered the call.
9. **A static, per-adapter caveat note is shown next to the sandbox/testing toggle's raw value**, documenting the known scope inconsistency from [[feedback_sandbox_flag_leaks_into_health_checks]] (e.g. "Digiflazz: testing mode does not apply to checkBalance"). A dynamic per-call-type "which mode will this actually run in" oracle was considered and rejected as overengineering for a tool serving 2 adapters today.
10. **New standalone page, `/middleware/developer-tools`** — not folded into `/middleware/suppliers`. The spec (§6.20) already lists MUI-11 as its own page, and its workflow (ad-hoc raw testing across suppliers) is a different concern from that screen's config/CRUD scope.
11. **No new permission tier** — standard `/middleware` admin auth already gates this whole area, and this is a solo-founder operation (AGENTS.md); the risk this tool carries is already bounded by decisions 3/4 (dry-run default, production `createOrder` block), not by who's allowed to open the page.

**Rationale:** Decision 2 is the load-bearing call — "raw JSON editor" could easily have meant a literal pass-through to the supplier's HTTP API, which would have quietly reintroduced exactly the kind of unvalidated-value-reaches-a-live-money-system risk this codebase's other conventions (money computed server-side, FormRequest validation at every mutating boundary) exist to prevent. Tying the editor to the existing typed DTOs gets the "raw" feel (admin sees and can change the exact JSON) without bypassing the one seam (`SupplierAdapter`) this whole integration layer is built around. Decision 4 is the second load-bearing call: unlike the other 4 methods, a real `createOrder` can cost real money or create a real fulfillment obligation on the supplier's side that this platform has no record of and no way to reconcile — a confirm dialog is adequate friction for a mistake, not for an action with an unrecoverable, un-tracked external consequence, so it's blocked structurally instead.

**Consequence to track:** if a third supplier adapter is ever added, decision 9's static caveat note needs a new per-adapter line rather than being assumed to generalize — [[feedback_sandbox_flag_leaks_into_health_checks]] already established this is adapter-specific, not a pattern. If this tool's `createOrder` block (decision 4) is ever found too restrictive in practice (e.g. the founder genuinely needs to test a production `createOrder` once CHIP/Digiflazz go live), revisit it as its own decision then — don't quietly loosen it as a side effect of unrelated work.

## ADR-055: Membership upsell promo card — storefront Order Summary, Tier 2 teaser (design only, grilled 2026-08-30; built 2026-08-30)

**Status:** Accepted (design) — 2026-08-30 (grilled with the founder via `/mattpocock-skills:grilling`, one question at a time, before any code touched). **Built 2026-08-30** — see the build addendum below; `docs/prd.md` §14/§15 updated same session.

**Context:** While live-testing this session's membership pricing fixes (this file's `ADR-027` 2026-08-30 addendum), the founder asked for a simple promo card below the storefront's Order Summary sidebar: "unlock {package} at {Tier 2 price}, save {%/RM}, subscribe for only {monthly fee}" — placeholders following whichever package the customer currently has selected. Investigation before grilling surfaced two real gaps this ADR had to resolve, not just a UI placement question:

1. **Tier 2's monthly fee (`fee_sen`) is 100% admin-only today.** `backend/routes/api.php`'s `membership-plans` prefix is gated `admin.role:super_admin` end to end — no route exposes any `MembershipPlan` field (`name`/`fee_sen`/`discount_percent`/`quota_sen`) publicly. The public catalog (`CatalogController::packages()`) already exposes a computed per-package `member_price_sen`/`member_price_personalized` (this session's earlier addendum) but never the raw plan fee itself.
2. **The storefront has no self-serve subscribe/pay flow at all.** `storefront/src/components/order/MembershipClient.tsx`'s own doc comment: "The 'subscribe' side of decision 4's two-tier flow isn't built yet (checkout wiring, ADR-027's own later phase) — a verified visitor with no active membership sees an honest 'coming soon' state here, not a fake subscribe form." The only way anyone becomes a member today is the founder manually recording payment in admin (`/admin/membership` Record Payment, ADR-027 Phase 6.5). ADR-027 Phase 7 (self-serve subscribe+pay) is explicitly unbuilt.

So the card's CTA had nowhere real to send a customer to actually complete a subscription — a genuine product decision, not an implementation detail, and the reason this got a full grill rather than being coded straight from the founder's rough copy.

**Decision:**

1. **Scope stays a display-only teaser — no self-serve subscribe/pay flow is built as part of this.** The card's CTA links to `/membership`'s existing "coming soon" messaging. Turning this into the trigger for Phase 7 (a real recurring/one-time membership-fee payment flow via Xendit/CHIP) was considered and explicitly rejected as its own, much larger scope — deserving its own dedicated grill when the founder is ready to build it, not absorbed silently into "add a card."
2. **Visibility:** hidden entirely when `PlatformSettings.membership_enabled` is off, and hidden for a customer already on Tier 2 (nothing left to upsell — showing it would be nonsensical). Shown for an anonymous guest and for a Tier 1 member, both cases always promoting **Tier 2** specifically (the top tier), matching the founder's own original wording.
3. **New public backend endpoint, `GET /api/membership/plans`** — deliberately separate from the existing admin-gated `membership-plans` prefix, not a reuse of it. Returns only `name`, `fee_sen`, `discount_percent` per tier (both Tier 1 and Tier 2, even though this card only needs Tier 2 — a direct reuse target for `/membership`'s own still-unbuilt Tier 1 vs Tier 2 comparison, ADR-027 decision 25). No `quota_sen`, `id`, or timestamp fields — narrower than what's plausibly useful later, on purpose (`AGENTS.md`'s "don't design for hypothetical future requirements"; add fields only when an actual consumer needs them). Empty/404 when `membership_enabled` is off.
4. **Savings shown per-package only, no break-even-after-N-purchases framing.** Matches the founder's own original wording exactly (a simple "save X now, subscription costs Y/month" pairing) — a break-even calculation was considered and rejected as unrequested complexity resting on an assumption (repeat-purchase frequency) this feature has no data to back.
5. **Card appears only once a package is selected** — its placeholders (`{package name}`, `{Tier 2 price}`, `{savings}`) have nothing to render before then. Lives in the same `OrderSummarySidebar` region as the Package Price/Transaction Fee/Total breakdown (this session's other addendum), appearing at the same point those rows start rendering.
6. **One copy template, not two — only the CTA phrase swaps by audience.** Guest: "Become a Member." Tier 1 member: "Upgrade to Tier 2." Everything else in the card (package name, Tier 2 price, savings, fee) renders identically for both audiences.
7. **Plumbing:** fetched server-side in `order/[slug]/page.tsx` alongside the existing `getGame`/`getGamePackages`/`listPaymentChannels` calls, not a separate client-side round trip. Cached with the same 60s TTL/tagged-store discipline as `CatalogController`'s own public endpoints (`ADR-014`), invalidated from the same write path that already flushes `catalog.packages` on a membership plan edit (`CatalogController::forgetPackagesCacheForMembership()`).
8. **Ships as its own branch/PR off `staging`**, not folded into the `fix/membership-tier-markup-and-record-payment-ui` branch this session's bug fixes and the Package Price/Transaction Fee breakdown shipped on — this is a genuinely new feature surface, not a fix, and that branch already carries four stacked pieces of work from one session.

**Rationale:** Decision 1 is the load-bearing call — the founder's rough ask ("add a simple card") could have silently absorbed a full payment-flow feature (Phase 7) if the CTA had been built to actually complete a subscription; scoping it to a teaser keeps this session's actual ask (a display element) from ballooning into unplanned payment-integration work. Decision 3's new public endpoint (rather than loosening the existing admin-gated one, or inlining `fee_sen` into the catalog packages response) keeps the admin-only `membership-plans` routes untouched and gives `/membership`'s own known-incomplete comparison UI (decision 25 of `ADR-027`'s earlier addendum) a ready-made data source instead of a second one being built later for the same need.

**Consequence to track:**
- This ADR is design-only — no code exists yet. Implementation (backend endpoint, storefront card component, `docs/prd.md` §14/§15 update) is deferred to a future session, per the founder's own instruction this session.
- If Phase 7 (self-serve subscribe+pay) is ever scoped, decision 1's teaser-only framing for this card should be revisited then — the CTA may be worth pointing at a real subscribe flow instead of `/membership`'s "coming soon" state once one exists.
- Decision 3's new endpoint returning both tiers (not just Tier 2) is unused surplus until `/membership`'s own comparison UI is actually built — acceptable since it's the same data shape either consumer needs, not speculative scope beyond what's already decided to expose.

**Addendum, 2026-08-30 — built, all eight decisions implemented as designed.** Shipped on `feature/adr-055-membership-upsell-card` (decision 8's own branch, off `staging`).

*Backend:*
- `MembershipController::plans()` + `GET /api/membership/plans` (public, no session token). Returns both tiers' `{name, fee_sen, discount_percent}` only (decision 3 — no `quota_sen`/`id`/timestamps), `[]` when `membership_enabled` is off — resolved the ADR's open "Empty/404" in favor of **Empty** (`[]`, 200): a single contract shape the storefront renders as "no card" without a 404 special case, matching the codebase's narrow-response-shape discipline.
- Cached in the existing `catalog_packages_store` (redis, 60s TTL), tagged `catalog.packages` — so `CatalogController::forgetPackagesCacheForMembership()`, already flushed on every `membership_plans` edit and kill-switch toggle, invalidates this endpoint for free (decision 7).

*Storefront:*
- `lib/membership.ts`: `listPlans()` + `MembershipPlan` type (zod, ADR-044).
- `order/[slug]/page.tsx`: `listPlans()` fetched server-side alongside `getGamePackages`/`listPaymentChannels`, passed down (decision 7 — no client round trip).
- `OrderForm.tsx`: audience detection — the existing membership-token effect now also calls `getMe(token)` to learn the visitor's own tier (keyed by token like the personalized-packages state, so a guest/SSR render reads back null without setState-in-effect). 
- `OrderSummarySidebar.tsx`: unchanged back to its pre-card state — the promo is its own card, not a section inside it. `OrderForm.tsx` resolves the visibility and renders `MembershipPromoCard` as a **separate rounded card in the same right-hand column, below the Order Summary card** (founder's own placement call after seeing it inside the card) — visible only once a package is selected, hidden when plans are empty (kill switch off) or the visitor is already on the top tier (decision 2). Top tier resolved by max `discount_percent`, robust against admin renaming a tier's `name`. One copy template, CTA phrase swaps by audience — "Become a Member" (guest) vs "Upgrade to Tier 2" (Tier 1), decision 6. CTA links to `/membership` (decision 1 — teaser only, no Phase 7 scope).

*Implementation nuance worth recording (not in the original decisions):* the card always promotes Tier 2, but a Tier 1 member's `packages` prop is personalized to their own tier — so the card's Tier 2 member price is sourced from the **anonymous SSR anchor** (`initialPackages`, always the best-tier price) rather than the personalized package list. Both displayed numbers remain backend-computed (ORD-9); the savings row is a pure render of two server-provided values.

*Tests:* 3 new `MembershipControllerTest` cases (empty-when-disabled, narrow-tier-shape-when-enabled, and cache-invalidation-via-`forgetPackagesCacheForMembership`). Full backend suite **1063/1063 green**. `npx tsc --noEmit`/`eslint`/`next build` clean on `storefront/`.

**Consequence to track (this addendum):** the original "not yet built" consequence bullet above is superseded — the card is live on the feature branch; only decision 1's Phase-7 revisit and decision 3's unused-surplus note remain, unchanged in kind.

## ADR-056: Reseller wholesale pricing & subscription tiers — `reseller_membership_tiers`, cost-anchored wholesale rate, tier fee from earnings

**Status:** Accepted (design) — 2026-08-30 (grilled with the founder via `/mattpocock-skills:grilling`, six rounds, before any code touched — the design tree covered premise, scope boundary, transaction channel, money model, auth, domain routing, and phasing)

**Context:**
- `ADR-027`'s 2026-08-29 continued addendum (decisions 8–16) settled the *shape* of reseller wholesale pricing — a paid `reseller_membership_tiers` subscription, cost-anchored, fully decoupled from consumer VIP Membership — but recorded it design-only and "fully re-arguable at build time." This ADR is that re-argument plus the build spec, split across ADR-056..060 (see the phasing note at the end).
- **A real third-party reseller is confirmed to be onboarding** (founder, this session) — this is no longer speculative Phase 2 groundwork, which is why the scope is "full Phase 2" (staged), not the minimal accounting-only cut.
- Facts confirmed against code this session: `reseller_membership_tiers` is fully greenfield (no migration, no model, no UI). `PricingService::calculate()` already takes a `$resellerMarkupPct` parameter but the platform owner passes `0` — no reseller-tier branch exists. `Reseller` carries `markup_pct` / `max_markup_pct` / `xendit_subaccount_id` columns unused in pricing today. `package.markup_percent` is set via `/admin/games` (`PackageController::updateMarkup()`) and Platform Settings bulk (`SettingsController::bulkMarkup()`), both recompute the **stored** `standard_selling_price` via `PackageMarkupService`; `cost_price` is supplier-sync-only. `ledger_entries` / `ledger_accounts` (ADR-002) key on polymorphic `owner_type` / `owner_id` — a reseller as a ledger owner needs no schema change. `LedgerService::credit()` is lock-free (additions can't fail); `withdraw()` locks the `ledger_accounts` mutex row.
- The founder's mental model, stated this session: **platform : reseller ∷ Gamevion : platform** — the platform is a "supplier" to its resellers the same way Gamevion is a supplier to the platform. The one difference the founder named: the platform *provides the reseller a storefront*, whereas Gamevion only provides API docs plus its own dashboard.

**Decision:**

1. **New table `reseller_membership_tiers`** — `id`, `name`, `monthly_fee_sen` (integer sen), `markup_percent` (decimal, applied over `cost_price`), `is_active`, `sort_order`, timestamps. **Admin CRUD, add/edit/remove freely** — not locked at a fixed row count. (`membership_plans`' exactly-2-row lock exists only for the consumer anchor/decoy psychology of `ADR-027` decision 4; no equivalent constraint applies to a B2B rate ladder, and the founder wants to add tiers as the reseller base grows.)

2. **A reseller's effective wholesale base price = `cost_price × (1 + tier.markup_percent / 100)`** for their currently-active paid tier. Computed live per order (ORD-9), never stored. Anchored on **supplier `cost_price`**, never on `standard_selling_price` and never on `package.markup_percent` — the two markup systems stay fully independent. `tier.markup_percent` and `package.markup_percent` are different numbers set on different screens for different buyer relationships.

3. **No active tier ⇒ the base falls back to `standard_selling_price`** (`cost_price × (1 + package.markup_percent / 100)` — the same price a guest pays at the platform's own storefront). "No active tier" = never subscribed, or lapsed past the grace period (decision 6). This is **not a shutdown or a penalty**: the reseller's storefront stays live, their own `markup_pct` still applies, they simply get the walk-in wholesale rate, and it self-corrects the moment they pay the fee. The founder reasoned the economics through explicitly this session and they are recorded here on purpose: when a tier lapses, the platform captures the **full** retail margin (`standard_selling_price − cost_price`) instead of the thin tier margin, and the reseller's customer-facing prices rise (less competitive) while the reseller still earns their own markup on the higher base.

4. **`Reseller.markup_pct` / `max_markup_pct` keep their existing meaning, unchanged** (`ADR-027` decision 16) — the reseller's own downstream margin, applied on top of the effective wholesale base: **`customer_price = effective_base × (1 + reseller.markup_pct / 100)`**, multiplicative, consistent with `PricingService`. Constrained `0 ≤ markup_pct ≤ max_markup_pct`; `max_markup_pct` is admin-set per reseller.

5. **Best-tier floor ≈ 3% `markup_percent`, admin-editable, not a hardcoded constant.** Unlike the consumer floor (`ADR-027` decision 5, 0%, justified by the hard monthly quota capping platform exposure per member), reseller volume is unlimited — a 0% floor would leave the flat monthly fee as the only per-unit profit at any scale. Both floors (consumer 0%, reseller ~3%) live in admin-editable config, in one place, so neither is a magic constant and they're not managed in two screens.

6. **The monthly tier fee is charged against the reseller's earnings ledger balance** — there is no prepaid deposit wallet in this ADR's scope (decision 7). `ChargeResellerTierFeesCommand` (scheduled, mirrors `ResetMembershipCyclesCommand`; inert until a real cron runs, so locally it's a manual `artisan` call) debits `monthly_fee_sen` from the reseller's earnings account on the tier cycle date and writes a `reseller_tier_fee` ledger entry (`ADR-027` decision 15's named type, now real). If earnings are insufficient, a **~3-day grace period** starts (matching `ADR-027` decision 13 — a manual-collection stopgap can lag for reasons unrelated to intent to pay); past grace with the fee still unpaid, the tier lapses to decision 3's fallback. An admin can also record or trigger the charge manually.

7. **No prepaid deposit wallet, no top-up flow, in this ADR (or this staged build at all).** In the storefront channel (ADR-060) the platform collects retail directly, so a reseller never needs to pre-fund anything to transact — earnings simply accrue. A prepaid wallet plus top-up (manual first, CHIP-backed later) belongs to the future **API / H2H channel** (a reseller pulling supply for their own off-platform site — the true Gamevion-mirror), and will be designed in that channel's own ADR, where it is mandatory rather than infrastructure for a mechanism that doesn't exist yet. This keeps the near-term build to a **single reseller ledger account (earnings only)**.

8. **Manual fee-collection stopgap, same as consumer membership** — no payment-gateway automation for the tier fee now; the fee is booked as a ledger entry when earnings are debited (decision 6). Upgrade to an invoiced/automated flow later if reseller volume justifies it; `MembershipFeeService`'s single-seam pattern is the reference.

9. **`reseller_tier_fee` and `membership_fee` stay two distinct ledger types** (`ADR-027` decision 15, unchanged) — a recurring small-value consumer subscription and a small number of larger B2B monthly payments have different reporting dynamics; one discriminated type just pushes the split into every report query.

10. **This ADR is backend-only.** Admin CRUD for tiers lands with ADR-058 (admin Reseller Management); the pricing branch is exercised by ADR-060 (branded storefront). But the tier schema/model, the `PricingService` reseller branch, the `reseller_tier_fee` type, `ChargeResellerTierFeesCommand`, and the grace/lapse state machine all ship here, testable in isolation (unit tests on the pricing math; a concurrency test on the earnings debit reusing the `LedgerWithdrawConcurrencyTest` two-process pattern). **No dependency on production deployment.**

**Rationale:** Decision 2 (anchor on `cost_price`, not `standard_selling_price`) is load-bearing — it is exactly the reconciliation `ADR-027`'s addendum spent a full grill reaching, and getting it wrong reintroduces the margin-stacking failure that killed the referral-tier proposal. Decision 7 (no wallet yet) is the other load-bearing call: the founder's first instinct was "prepaid wallet, like our own Gamevion deposit," but the storefront channel *inverts* the money flow (the platform collects retail), so the wallet has no job until the API channel exists — building it now would be the "setting for a mechanism that doesn't exist yet" anti-pattern this codebase has deliberately avoided in `ADR-015` / `ADR-016` / `ADR-020` / `ADR-028` / `ADR-029`. Decision 6 (fee from earnings) follows directly from 7 — with no deposit balance, earnings is the only reseller-held balance to charge against.

**Consequence to track:**
- ~~Design-only, no code.~~ **Backend built + merged 2026-08-30 (PR #28).** Admin CRUD shipped ADR-058 58b. Checkout wiring is ADR-060.
- Decision 5's floors need a real home in admin config — pick `platform_settings` vs a dedicated row at build time, and surface consumer + reseller floors together.
- When the API / H2H channel is scoped, revisit decision 7: the prepaid wallet arrives then, which means a reseller will have **two** balances (deposit + earnings) and `LedgerService` will need an account discriminator beyond `owner_type` / `owner_id` (both accounts belong to the same `Reseller`). Design that discriminator then, not now.
- Decision 3's lapse economics assume `package.markup_percent` > `tier.markup_percent` for every package (so the fallback is genuinely a worse rate for the reseller). If an admin ever sets a package markup below a reseller tier rate, that framing breaks — worth a validation warning at build time.
- `reseller_tier_fee` is a real ledger type now; its report line (template: the consumer `membership_fee` line, `ADR-027` Phase 6.5) is still owed on the admin Reports surface.
- PRD deltas — **applied** (§13 Glossary `Reseller Wholesale Tier`, §8 `Reseller`/`Package` rows, §14/§15, ORD-9).

## ADR-057: Tenant isolation mechanism — `BelongsToReseller` trait + Eloquent global scope, retrofitted before any reseller-scoped endpoint

**Status:** Accepted — built + merged 2026-08-30 (design grilled with the founder via `/mattpocock-skills:grilling`, same session as ADR-056).

**Built:** `App\Support\CurrentReseller` (`scoped` binding — reset per request/job, populated by the ADR-058 middleware, inert everywhere else); `App\Models\Scopes\ResellerScope` (not-active → unconstrained; active + id → `where reseller_id`; active + no id → `where 1=0` fail-closed; `runWithout()` bypass); `App\Models\Concerns\BelongsToReseller` trait (boots the scope, provides `reseller()` + `withoutResellerScope()`). Trait applied to `Order`, `ResellerBranding`, `ResellerFooterSettings`, `ResellerSeoSettings`, `Redirect` (their duplicate `reseller()` methods removed). `SeoScript` excluded — its `null reseller_id` means "global", which a `= <id>` scope would wrongly hide, and it is admin-only. Migration `2026_08_30_110000_add_reseller_id_index_and_backfill_orders`: standalone `orders.reseller_id` index (guarded — SQLite never auto-indexes the FK; MySQL's `orders_reseller_id_foreign` already covers it) + NULL→`platformOwner` backfill (only resolved when rows actually need it). `tests/Feature/Database/ResellerScopeTest.php` proves (a)/(b)/(c)/(d) across all five models + both escape hatches. 1085/1085 fast + 10/10 concurrency.

**Deviation from decision 2 (resolved):** `orders.reseller_id` shipped **nullable** here — flipping it in this PR would have turned a focused isolation change into a suite-wide fixture refactor. The scope fails closed on reads regardless, so a tenant-less row is invisible under the reseller guard. **Resolved in [ADR-061](#adr-061-every-storefront-is-a-reseller--abolish-the-platform-owner-special-case) PR-B (2026-08-31):** `OrderFactory` added, column flipped to NOT NULL, FK `nullOnDelete()` → `restrictOnDelete()` (SET NULL is illegal on a NOT NULL column in MySQL).

**Context:**
- `ADR-003` (2026-07-23) decided "tenant scoping enforced via ORM global scopes, not per-query convention" and "`reseller_id` as a first-class column, tenant scoping enforced via ORM global scopes." Confirmed against code this session: **neither was actually built.** `orders.reseller_id` is a plain nullable, unconstrained column; only `orders`, `reseller_branding`, `reseller_footer_settings`, `reseller_seo_settings`, `redirects`, `seo_scripts` carry `reseller_id` at all; there is no global scope, no trait, no tenant middleware anywhere in `app/`.
- Every reseller-scoped read in the coming portal (ADR-059) — "my orders", "my earnings", "my customers" — is a cross-tenant data-leak vector if scoping is left to per-query discipline, which is exactly the risk `ADR-003`'s own rationale named ("a single missed `WHERE` clause becomes a cross-tenant data leak").
- This must land **before** any reseller-guard endpoint that returns tenant data — it is the hard prerequisite for ADR-059.

**Decision:**

1. **`BelongsToReseller` trait** — adds a `reseller()` `BelongsTo` and boots an Eloquent **global scope** that constrains queries to the current tenant when a reseller-guard session is active (`auth('reseller')->check()`), and applies **no constraint** for the platform/admin guards, the console, and queue jobs (which legitimately operate across all tenants). The "current reseller" is resolved from the authenticated `reseller_user`'s `reseller_id` (ADR-058) held in a request-scoped resolver — **never from a request parameter**.

2. **Add a real `reseller_id` FK + standalone index to `orders`** (currently unconstrained per that migration's own note — `foreignId()->constrained()` has been found once in this codebase to not reliably leave a standalone index, so verify via `SHOW INDEX`), backfilled to the `Reseller::platformOwner()` row for every existing row (`ADR-013` — every existing order genuinely is the platform owner's). `ledger_entries` / `withdrawals` already key on polymorphic `owner_type` / `owner_id`, so an earnings account is already reseller-owned with no column change (see the consequence note). Any new reseller-owned table (ADR-058/059/060) uses the trait from creation.

3. **The scope is deny-by-default for the reseller guard** — a model using the trait with no resolvable current reseller under the reseller guard returns **zero rows, never all rows**. A missing tenant context is a bug that fails closed.

4. **Admin / platform code paths are explicitly unscoped** — `/admin/orders` showing every reseller's orders labelled per-reseller (founder, this session) works because the admin guard applies no constraint. Where an admin needs to act *as* one reseller (impersonation, ADR-058 RES-4), that runs under a real reseller-guard token, so the same scope applies automatically.

5. **A `withoutResellerScope()` escape hatch** exists for the rare legitimate cross-tenant query under a reseller context (there are none planned; it exists so a future need doesn't tempt a raw query that bypasses the trait entirely).

6. **The retrofit is its own PR, with a test per newly-scoped model** proving: (a) a reseller session sees only its own rows, (b) the admin session sees all, (c) a queue job sees all, (d) no tenant context under the reseller guard sees none.

**Rationale:** A global scope keyed off the *guard* (not a parameter, not a per-query `where`) is the only approach that makes the safe path the default and the unsafe path something you have to write on purpose — which is what `ADR-003` was aiming at and didn't reach. Deny-by-default (decision 3) matters because the failure mode of "fail open" here is a silent cross-tenant financial-data leak, the worst outcome this system can produce short of losing money.

**Consequence to track:**
- Hard prerequisite for ADR-059 — done, sequenced before it. No dependency on production deployment.
- `ADR-003`'s status note updated (2026-08-30) — its "schema tenant-aware from day 1" claim is now marked partially superseded.
- `orders.reseller_id` NOT NULL — **done in ADR-061 PR-B (2026-08-31)**, along with the `OrderFactory` it was waiting on.
- `CurrentReseller` lifecycle is owned by the ADR-058 reseller-guard middleware: it `activate()`s on the way in and the `scoped` binding handles teardown. Shipped in ADR-058 58a.
- Global scopes are trivially bypassed with `DB::table()` / raw queries — a grep for `DB::table(` in reseller-context code belongs on the ADR-059 review checklist.
- The polymorphic `owner_type` / `owner_id` ledger design means `ledger_entries` itself does **not** use the trait (it has no `reseller_id`). Reseller-scoped ledger reads must go through a service that filters `owner_type = 'reseller', owner_id = <current>` explicitly (`ResellerEarningsService`, ADR-059). Document that seam so it's not mistaken for an unscoped gap. **Note (2026-08-30 review):** `owner_type` is the literal string `'reseller'` in code (`LedgerService`, `OrderFulfillmentService::creditProfit()`, `ResellerTierFeeService`) — **not** `Reseller::class`. `ResellerEarningsService` must filter on `'reseller'`. A `LedgerOwnerType` enum to replace these string literals at a money seam is recommended before ADR-059 writes that service (see the post-ADR-057 review addendum on ADR-060).

## ADR-058: Reseller authentication + admin Reseller Management (RES-1..6)

**Status:** Accepted (design) — 2026-08-30 (grilled with the founder via `/mattpocock-skills:grilling`, same session as ADR-056)

**Context:**
- No non-admin authentication exists anywhere. `config/auth.php` has one guard (`web`, session, `admin_users` provider); `admin_users.role` is `super_admin | admin`; `admin/` uses Sanctum bearer tokens against that.
- RES-1..6 (PRD §6.7) specify admin reseller CRUD + impersonation, all Phase 2, all unbuilt.
- The reseller portal (ADR-059) needs its own login. Founder decision this session: a **separate reseller portal with its own auth**, and **`/admin` also gets a Reseller Management tab** to register resellers, view their details, and route their domain.
- `PlunkMailer` (`ADR-027`) exists and is wired for transactional email (sender-domain verification still `Pending`).

**Decision:**

1. **New guard `reseller` + provider `reseller_users`** in `config/auth.php`, Sanctum bearer tokens (same mechanism as admin, separate guard). New table `reseller_users` — `id`, `reseller_id` (FK), `name`, `email` (unique), `password`, `is_active`, `last_login_at`, timestamps. One reseller can have multiple staff users from day one — the schema supports it even if the first onboarding creates exactly one.

2. **Resellers never self-register.** An admin creates the `Reseller` row and its first `reseller_user` in `/admin`, and the system emails a **set-password invitation** (Plunk, signed expiring link, mirroring a standard password-reset token flow). Matches PRD's standing "no reseller self-service onboarding" Phase 2 deferral — onboarding is admin-driven; only the password step is the reseller's.

3. **Admin Reseller Management screen (`/admin`, `super_admin` only** — same tier as Settings / Price Sync / Membership config). Covers:
   - **RES-1**: reseller table — business name, contact, active tier + subscription status, earnings balance, orders count, domain status, status, actions.
   - **RES-2**: add reseller — business info, `markup_pct` + `max_markup_pct`, assign initial `reseller_membership_tier`, create first `reseller_user` (triggers decision 2's invite).
   - **RES-3**: edit reseller details, change `max_markup_pct`, change tier (writes a tier-change audit row).
   - **RES-5**: activate / deactivate — deactivate ⇒ the ADR-060 storefront returns 503 and the Cloudflare custom hostname is suspended; existing earnings stay withdrawable; no new orders.
   - **RES-6**: delete — **soft-delete only** (FK on `orders`; history must survive), allowed only when earnings balance = 0 and there is no pending withdrawal; the Cloudflare custom hostname is removed.
   - **`reseller_membership_tiers` CRUD** (ADR-056's admin surface) — its own section on this screen, same `super_admin` gate.
   - Record a manual tier-fee payment / trigger a tier charge (ADR-056 decisions 6/8).
4. **Impersonation (RES-4)** — an admin action that mints a short-lived `reseller`-guard Sanctum token scoped to the target reseller and opens the reseller portal (ADR-059) in an impersonation session. Every request in that session is tagged with the real admin identity + session start/end; the portal shows a persistent "Impersonating {reseller} — acting as {admin}" banner; an audit row is written on start and end. Because the session runs under the real `reseller` guard, `ADR-057`'s tenant scope applies automatically — an impersonating admin sees exactly what the reseller sees, nothing cross-tenant.

5. **No maker-checker on reseller CRUD** — solo-founder workflow (`AGENTS.md`); the `super_admin` gate + audit rows are sufficient. Withdrawals (ADR-059) keep the existing WTH maker-checker because that moves money out.

6. **Reseller-guard routes get their own throttle prefix from day one** (`throttle:*,*,reseller-login`, etc.) — `ADR-021`'s addendum documents the shared-throttle-bucket bug class this codebase has already hit twice.

7. **PrimeReact-Tailwind for every new admin screen** (`ADR-038`) — no hand-rolled TailAdmin primitives in Reseller Management.

**Rationale:** A fully separate guard + user table (decision 1) rather than a third `admin_users.role` keeps the money-critical admin surface and the reseller surface from sharing a session, a token namespace, or a component set where a role check could be missed — the security boundary is worth the extra table. Decision 2 (admin-created, invite to set password) keeps onboarding controlled without the admin ever handling a plaintext password.

**Consequence to track:**
- Design-only. Depends on ADR-057 (the reseller guard is what activates the tenant scope). No dependency on production deployment.
- Sanctum's guard/ability model needs checking at build time — token abilities may be a cleaner way to scope an impersonation token than guard config alone; resolve against the installed Sanctum version's docs, not assumption.
- `foundation-security.md` §1's MFA-before-money-actions mandate is already unmet for admins (`ADR-020` notes it); a reseller portal that can request withdrawals raises the same question for `reseller_users`. Flag it — founder call, not silently skipped.
- The set-password invite reuses Plunk, still pending sender-domain verification (`ADR-027`). Reseller onboarding email is blocked on the same external step as consumer OTP.

**Build addendum — 2026-08-30 (founder decisions):**
- **Split into two PRs.** ADR-058 is unusually large (a guard, `reseller_users`, two audit tables, ~8 admin endpoints, a full PrimeReact screen, impersonation, an invite email). **58a** = the auth foundation, backend only: the `reseller` guard + `reseller_users` + `ResellerUser` model + the `SetResellerContext` middleware that calls `CurrentReseller::activate()` (this is what actually switches on `ADR-057`'s scope in production) + reseller login / set-password / logout / me + reseller-route throttle buckets. **58b** = admin Reseller Management: RES-1..6 endpoints, `reseller_membership_tiers` CRUD, the manual tier-fee record/charge action, RES-4 impersonation (+ its audit table), the Plunk invite send, and the `admin/src/app/admin/resellers/` screen. `resellers.deleted_at` (soft-delete) + the tier-change audit table land in 58b with the features that use them.
- **MFA for `reseller_users`: deferred**, matching the already-unmet admin MFA gap (`ADR-020`, `foundation-security.md` §1). The portal withdrawal path keeps the existing WTH maker-checker (an admin approves every payout) as the compensating control. Recorded as known security debt — resolve alongside the admin MFA gap, not separately.
- **Sanctum guard mechanics:** 58a defines `reseller` as a `driver => 'sanctum'` guard with its own `reseller_users` provider; `auth:reseller` must reject an `admin_users` token (and vice versa). Verify the installed Sanctum v4 tokenable-provider check does this and pin it with a test — do not assume `auth:sanctum` alone separates the two surfaces.
- **`ResellerUser` does NOT use `BelongsToReseller`** (unlike every other reseller-owned table): it is only ever queried by email at login (no tenant context), by Sanctum as the token's `tokenable` (which must not be tenant-constrained or auth resolution breaks), and by the admin (cross-tenant). No reseller-facing "manage my team" query path exists yet. Revisit when ADR-059+ adds one, with a scope that is provably safe against the tokenable load.

**Built — 58b, 2026-08-30 (`feature/adr-058b-reseller-management`):**
- **RES-1..6 + tier CRUD, all on `/admin/resellers`, `super_admin` only.** `Admin\ResellerController` (list with a batched `LedgerService::balances()` earnings query; create = reseller + first `reseller_user` + optional initial tier + Plunk invite in one transaction that rolls back on a Plunk failure; edit; `assignTier` / `chargeTierFee` / `reactivateSubscription`; `storeUser` / `resendInvite`; `updateStatus`; soft-delete `destroy`). `Admin\ResellerMembershipTierController` (CRUD). `Admin\ResellerImpersonationController` (RES-4).
- **`reseller_membership_tiers` + `resellers` gained `deleted_at` (soft-delete).** A hard delete of a tier any reseller was ever subscribed to is impossible (`reseller_subscriptions.reseller_membership_tier_id` is `restrictOnDelete`); soft-delete keeps historical subscription/audit rows resolvable. The controller additionally **blocks** deleting a tier with an `active`/`grace` subscriber outright. Reseller delete is blocked unless earnings balance = 0 **and** no `pending`/`approved` withdrawal, and the `Platform Owner` row can never be deleted.
- **New audit tables.** `reseller_tier_changes` (append-only, one row per tier assignment/change, both tier FKs `nullOnDelete`, `membership_plan_changes` precedent). `reseller_impersonation_sessions` (real `admin_user_id` + `reseller_user_id` it acts as + `personal_access_token_id` `nullOnDelete` + `started_at` / `ended_at` / `ended_reason`).
- **`ResellerSubscriptionService`** — the new admin-side seam for tier assignment + reactivation (writes the audit row); billing (fee charge, grace/lapse) stays entirely in ADR-056's `ResellerTierFeeService`. `reactivate()` sets `active` + a fresh 30-day cycle, no immediate charge.
- **Impersonation token mechanics (the ADR's open question, resolved).** Sanctum v4's `createToken($name, $abilities, $expiresAt)` 3-arg form is used: a token with abilities `['impersonate']` and a 60-minute expiry, minted against the reseller's first invite-accepted active `reseller_user`. The session runs under the real `reseller` guard so ADR-057's tenant scope applies unchanged. Ending a session (or deactivating/deleting the reseller) deletes the `personal_access_tokens` row and closes the audit row. **Deferred to ADR-059:** the persistent "Impersonating {reseller} — acting as {admin}" banner and per-request admin tagging (the portal app doesn't exist yet — 58b's UI shows the minted token + portal URL inline as a stopgap).
- **`ResellerInviteService::sendInvite()`** added (58a built only `createInviteLink()`). `PlunkMailer` gained a generic `send($to, $subject, $body)` primitive; `sendOtpEmail()` now delegates to it.
- **Admin UI:** `admin/src/app/admin/resellers/page.tsx` + `lib/resellers.ts` + `components/resellers/{ResellerFormModal,ResellerDetailModal,ResellerTierFormModal}.tsx`, PrimeReact-Tailwind only (new screen). Sidebar nav item added.
- **Not wired (ADR-059/060):** Cloudflare custom-hostname create/suspend/remove on domain add / RES-5 / RES-6 — `domains` is stored as a plain string list for now. `LedgerOwnerType` enum (the 2026-08-30 review's finding 3) still deferred to ADR-059's `ResellerEarningsService`.
- **`RESELLER_PORTAL_URL` still owed in `backend/.env.example`** (file not editable in the 58a or 58b session — default `http://localhost:3002` in `config/services.php`).
- 26 new tests; backend **1127/1127** fast + **10/10** concurrency; admin `tsc`/`eslint`/`build` clean; Pint clean.
- **Live-verified in Chrome** against the real Herd backend + admin dev server (founder logged in — automated password entry is disallowed in this environment): full walk of tier CRUD, reseller create (Plunk invite genuinely delivered), tier assign + audit, charge-fee → grace (no ledger write) → fund → charge → active (`reseller_tier_fee` −4900), impersonate → token (`abilities=["impersonate"]`, 1h expiry) + audit → End (token revoked), all three delete guards, soft-delete. **Two bugs found + fixed same session:** the on-page impersonation-sessions list didn't refresh after starting one (`onRefresh` callback added); a soft-deleted reseller's lingering `reseller_subscriptions` row still counted toward a tier's subscriber total and blocked deleting that tier (`ResellerMembershipTierController` now filters `whereHas('reseller')`, +1 test).

**Build addendum — `/set-password` frontend page, grilled 2026-09-05 (gap found the day PR-G's invite links were fixed).** Decision 2's invite email always pointed at `/set-password?token=...&email=...` — a page that has never existed on the `reseller/` app, for either an `Affiliate` or a `Reseller` (wallet) account, since this ADR shipped. The backend half (`POST /api/affiliate/set-password`, `AffiliateAuthController::setPassword()`) was built and tested from day one; only the frontend acceptance page was missed, silently, until a real invite link was clicked. Grilled 1 round (all resolved, no new decision — this is completing an already-specified contract, not opening one):

1. **Error handling accepts the backend's actual granularity, no better.** Laravel's `PasswordBroker` collapses "wrong token", "expired token" (24h TTL, `config/auth.php`), and "already-used token" into one identical response (`422`, `passwords.token` on the `email` field) — there is no way to distinguish them server-side, and building a distinguishing UI would be fake precision. The page shows one generic message: "Link tidak sah atau sudah tamat tempoh. Sila hubungi admin untuk hantar invite baharu." for any `errors.email` response, and the field-level `errors.password` message (weak/mismatched) verbatim for that case.
2. **No Route Handler proxy** — unlike `/login` (which calls `/api/login` through a same-origin Next.js Route Handler because that call sets a session cookie), `set-password` has no server-side state to set. The page calls `POST /api/affiliate/set-password` directly via the portal's existing `apiFetch` helper.
3. **Success flow**: on `200`, redirect to `/login?message=Password+berjaya+ditetapkan` (no auto-login — the endpoint returns no token, and adding one would be new backend scope for a gap-closing PR).
4. **No `owner_type` branching** — confirmed the broker operates purely on `affiliate_users` rows by email/token, with zero visibility into that row's polymorphic `owner_type`/`owner_id` (ADR-072 decision 5). One page serves both an `Affiliate` and a `Reseller` (wallet) invite identically, mirroring `/login`'s existing shared-page precedent.

**Shape:** one `reseller/src/app/set-password/page.tsx` — reads `token`+`email` off the query string, a password + confirm-password form (client-side `min 8` + match check before submit, mirroring the backend's own `min:8|confirmed` rule so a doomed request never round-trips), submits via `apiFetch`, redirects per decision 3 on success. `reseller/src/proxy.ts`'s `isEntryPoint` check gains `pathname === "/set-password"` alongside `/login`/`/impersonate`. No backend change — `AffiliateAuthController::setPassword()` already works, confirmed by direct code read this session, not assumed. Pure build from here — no further grilling needed.

**Built + shipped 2026-09-06** (`feature/adr-058-set-password-page`, PR #108 → staging → prod via release PR #110). Built exactly as the Shape above; `ApiError` gained an optional `errors` field so the page can tell an `errors.email` (bad/expired token) response from an `errors.password` one; `/login` renders the `?message=` success banner then strips it from the address bar. No backend change, no `reseller/` unit-test infra (build + lint + tsc green). **Live-verified in production 2026-09-06**: a real `/admin/resellers` invite link set a password and redirected to `/login` with the success banner; login then worked.
