## ADR-059: Reseller portal — `reseller/` app, earnings ledger, withdrawals, self-service storefront config

**Status:** Accepted (design) — 2026-08-30 (grilled with the founder via `/mattpocock-skills:grilling`, same session as ADR-056)

**Context:**
- The founder wants a dedicated reseller dashboard, separate from both `admin/` and `storefront/`.
- `ADR-028` / `ADR-029` already built `reseller_branding`, `reseller_footer_settings`, `reseller_seo_settings` as 1:1-with-`Reseller` tables with a `reseller_id` FK, **explicitly** so "a future real portal reuses the same tables/endpoints scoped to the reseller's own id, no schema change needed then" — that future is this ADR.
- `ledger_entries` / `withdrawals` polymorphic owner supports a `Reseller` owner with no schema change. `LedgerService::withdraw()` already serializes per-owner via the `ledger_accounts` mutex row (`ADR-002`).

**Decision:**

1. **New Next.js app `reseller/`** — a third app alongside `admin/` and `storefront/`, its own deploy target (originally a `docker-compose.prod.yml` service; **since [ADR-066](#adr-066-production-deploy-via-laravel-forge--reverses-adr-020s-docker-compose-containerisation) it is the `pekangame-reseller` Vercel project**). Auth via the `reseller` Sanctum guard (ADR-058). Its client-session hook mirrors `admin/`'s `useClientSession()` (including the `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` trap this codebase has hit — `ADR-038` decision 8, `ADR-027` Phase 5).

2. **Seven screens for the first build.** *(⚠️ Superseded by the 59c re-scope, 2026-08-31 — see the re-scope note under "Session decisions" below. The portal now ships in three PRs: 59a/59b = Dashboard / Orders / Earnings / Subscription (built); 59c = Withdrawal / Profile / Impersonation; **Storefront settings and Domain move to ADR-060**, where the branded storefront that consumes them is actually built.)*
   - **Dashboard** — earnings balance, today's / this-month's sales count and value, current tier + next charge date.
   - **Orders** — the reseller's own storefront orders (`ADR-057` scope), list + detail + delivery status. Read-only. No internal financial fields beyond the reseller's own margin (mirrors `backend/AGENTS.md`'s public-response discipline).
   - **Earnings / Ledger** — every `ledger_entries` row for `owner = this Reseller`: margin credits, withdrawal debits, `reseller_tier_fee` debits. Withdrawable balance = the current earnings balance (a single account — ADR-056 decision 7).
   - **Withdrawal** — request a payout against earnings; reuses the existing `Withdrawal` model + admin approve / reject / complete flow (WTH-1..5) with `owner_type = Reseller`. Maker-checker retained. Payout is manual bank transfer (decision 6).
   - **Storefront settings** — edit `reseller_branding` / `reseller_footer_settings` / `reseller_seo_settings` (expose the `ADR-028` / `ADR-029` tables under the reseller guard), set `markup_pct` within `[0, max_markup_pct]`, and toggle individual games on/off for the catalog (decision 3).
   - **Subscription** — current tier, fee, next charge date, payment/charge history, grace / lapse status.
   - **Domain** — custom-domain status and the exact DNS records to set (ADR-060).
   - The impersonation banner (ADR-058 decision 4) renders above every screen when active.

3. **Per-reseller catalog visibility** — a new table `reseller_game` (or a `reseller_disabled_games` list). Default: every active platform game is visible on every reseller storefront. A reseller can turn a game **fully off** for their storefront — no per-package granularity, no admin approval; the reseller controls their own shelf. ADR-060's storefront resolution respects it.

4. **`markup_pct` edits take effect on the next order only** — pricing is computed at order time (ORD-9); existing orders are untouched. The portal shows a **live preview** of a sample package's customer price at the entered markup before saving, reusing ADR-056's pricing service — the same "preview can't drift from what checkout actually charges" discipline as the membership Preview Pricing Impact button (`ADR-027` Phase 2).

5. **All reseller-portal money reads go through a tenant-scoped service layer**, never raw Eloquent on `ledger_entries` (which has no `reseller_id` — `ADR-057`'s consequence note). One `ResellerEarningsService` is the single seam.

6. **Withdrawal payout is manual bank transfer, permanently — this supersedes `ADR-001`'s xenPlatform-OWNED-sub-account addendum and `ADR-022` decision 2's "CHIP Send payout API" path for reseller payouts.** Founder decision this session: the platform will not use xenPlatform at all. All customer money — the platform owner's and every reseller storefront's — is collected into the **one company CHIP account**, and a reseller withdrawal is the admin transferring manually and marking the `Withdrawal` complete, exactly the WTH-1..5 flow that exists today for the platform owner. `Withdrawal.bank_name` / `bank_account_no` / `bank_account_holder` are already the right shape (`ADR-001`'s own consequence note anticipated this).

7. **No prepaid wallet / top-up screen** — ADR-056 decision 7. Added when the API / H2H channel is built.

**Rationale:** A separate app (decision 1) is the natural conclusion of ADR-058's separate-guard decision — the security boundary is cleaner if the reseller surface is also a separate deployable that physically cannot render an admin screen. Decision 6 is the big simplification this session bought: dropping xenPlatform removes sub-merchant KYC, the Disbursement API integration, the `for-user-id` plumbing, and the unresolved "is OWNED available in Malaysia" question — all replaced by "the admin does a bank transfer," which the platform already does for its own withdrawals and which `ADR-022` decision 2 already established is sufficient (the ledger, not the gateway, is the source of truth for who is owed what).

**Consequence to track:**
- Design-only. Depends on ADR-057 (tenant scope) and ADR-058 (reseller guard). Testable locally; the branded storefront it reports on is ADR-060, but the portal itself has no production dependency.
- `ADR-001`'s xenPlatform addendum and `ADR-022` decision 2's CHIP-Send path are **superseded for reseller payouts** by decision 6. xenPlatform is now out of the platform's plans entirely, not "deferred" — update the `xenPlatform` glossary entry and the `ADR-001` / `ADR-022` status notes when this ships.
- A third Next.js app adds CI time, a third `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` env surface, and a third app to keep on the same Next.js version — add `reseller/CLAUDE.md` with the same version warning `admin/` and `storefront/` carry.
- Reseller-facing withdrawal raises the MFA question for `reseller_users` (ADR-058 consequence) — resolve before this screen goes live.
- Decision 3's `reseller_game` toggle is the first per-tenant catalog-scoping table — it uses `BelongsToReseller` (`ADR-057`) from creation.
- **From the 2026-08-30 post-ADR-057 review:** `ResellerEarningsService` is the single seam for every reseller money read. It filters `ledger_entries` on `owner_type = 'reseller'` (string literal, see `ADR-057`'s consequence note) — never raw Eloquent on `ledger_entries`, never `DB::table('ledger_entries')`. Grep the finished portal for `DB::table(` in any reseller-guard code path before merge (this bypasses `ResellerScope` silently — `SupplierController` already has one benign admin-context instance). Consider introducing a `LedgerOwnerType` enum in this PR so the service is written against a type, not a magic string.

**Session decisions, 2026-08-31 (before building 59a — founder, `AskUserQuestion`):**

1. **MFA for `reseller_users` — descoped, matching admin.** Admin MFA (AUTH-7) was the founder's own explicit descope 2026-07-29; the reseller portal carries the same posture. What still gates a reseller payout: the WTH-1..5 maker-checker (`super_admin`, a different approver, at/above the RM-2,000 threshold) plus the reseller-login throttle bucket. Revisit alongside admin MFA if it is ever un-descoped. This removes the "resolve before this screen goes live" blocker above.
2. **Three PRs, not one.** **59a** = the backend **read layer** only. **59b** = the `reseller/` Next.js app scaffold + auth/session + the read-only screens (Dashboard / Orders / Earnings / Subscription). **59c** — originally "the write surface (storefront settings + catalog toggle + withdrawal)"; **re-scoped 2026-08-31 (see the 59c re-scope note below)** to just the parts that work end-to-end before ADR-060: **Withdrawal + Profile (bank details) + Impersonation entry & banner**.
3. **Domain screen deferred to ADR-060.** It shows Cloudflare custom-hostname status + DNS records, and none of that infrastructure exists until ADR-060 — so the screen and its endpoint land there.

**59c re-scope, 2026-08-31 (founder, `AskUserQuestion` + a reference-panel screenshot):**

Decision 2's "59c = storefront settings + catalog toggle + live preview" assumed the reseller portal configures a branded storefront that renders per reseller. It doesn't yet — **only `Reseller::primary()`'s storefront renders today**; per-`Host` branded storefronts are ADR-060 (unblocked 2026-09-02 — production is live — but not yet built). So a branding/markup/catalog editor in the portal now would be configuring a display that doesn't exist. The reference panel the founder wants to match (logo upload, per-reseller hero slideshow, a store theme) needs capabilities that also don't exist: `reseller_branding` is text-only (ADR-028 decision 2), `hero_slides` is global (no `reseller_id`), and the reseller **theme system is explicitly out of scope** (PRD §5 / §6.15 THM-1..4 are Phase 2, deferred to their own ADR).

- **59c ships the useful-now slice:** **Withdrawal** (a reseller has a real `('reseller', id)` earnings balance credited on every order since ADR-061 — a payout request is genuinely usable) + a **Profile** screen to store bank details on `resellers` (prefills the withdrawal form) + **Impersonation** entry (`/impersonate?token=` route consuming the ADR-058 RES-4 token, the admin side opening it, the persistent "Impersonating {reseller} — acting as {admin}" banner). Portal nav → 6 items (Dashboard / Orders / Earnings / Subscription / Withdrawal / Profile).
- **ADR-060 absorbs the storefront-config editors** — they take effect only once ADR-060 builds the per-`Host` branded storefront that reads them: the branding text editor (store name / description / support contacts / social links) **plus SEO pixel IDs (GA / FB / TikTok)** — the founder's answer: *pixel IDs are the only SEO field a reseller controls; meta templates / OG image / schema toggles stay admin-central via `{store_name}` substitution*; the `markup_pct` editor + live `PricingService::calculateForReseller()` preview; the `reseller_game` (or `reseller_disabled_games`) catalog on/off table + screen. Logo upload (a new `reseller_branding` column) and per-reseller hero slides (`hero_slides.reseller_id`) are open ADR-060 grilling questions, not assumed.
- **Footer & legal content stay admin-only, central.** `reseller_footer_settings` (footer text, `terms_content` / `privacy_content` / `about_us_content`, `footer_game_ids`) is edited only in `/admin`; every brand's storefront renders that one source with `{store_name}` substituted for the brand name (the substitution `BrandingController::substitute()` already does). **This supersedes the part of `ADR-028` / `ADR-029` that anticipated a reseller editing its own footer/legal rows** — legal text carries platform liability and the founder wants it centrally controlled. The per-`reseller_id` rows on those tables stay (schema unchanged); only the primary's row is authored, and ADR-060's `Host` resolution can fall back to it.
- **Reseller theme system stays deferred** to its own future ADR (unchanged — PRD §5 / §6.15).

**Build addendum — 59a shipped 2026-08-31** (`feature/adr-059a-reseller-portal-backend`). The read layer + the `LedgerOwnerType` enum. No `reseller/` app yet (59b), no write endpoints (59c).

- **`App\Services\Ledger\LedgerOwnerType`** (`Platform = 'platform'` / `Reseller = 'reseller'` — the literals persisted since ADR-002) + a `coerce(self|string)` normalizer that throws `\ValueError` on an unknown string. `LedgerService`'s public methods now accept `LedgerOwnerType|string` and normalize at the persistence boundary — **every existing caller keeps working unchanged**. Magic-string literals swapped for the enum at the money seams: `OrderFulfillmentService::creditProfit()`, `VoucherService::issue()`, `MembershipFeeService::bookFee()`, `ResellerTierFeeService`, `WithdrawalController`, `ResellerController` (earnings reads), `ReportService`, `CustomerAnalyticsService`. `LedgerEntryType` (the `order_profit` / `withdrawal` / … `type` column) is **not** in scope — a separate enum if ever wanted.
- **`App\Services\Reseller\ResellerEarningsService`** — the single seam (decision 5). `balance()` / `ledgerEntries()` (paginated, shaped — no `created_by`, no `owner_id`) / `tierFeeHistory()` / `dashboardStats()` (earnings balance + today's & this-month's paid-sales count/value on KL day boundaries, same `payment_status=Paid` / `paid_at` / `is_test=false` rules as `ReportService` + the subscription snapshot). Every read filters `owner_type` / `owner_id` explicitly against the `Reseller` passed in.
- **Endpoints** under `/api/reseller/*` (`auth:reseller` + `reseller.context`): `GET /dashboard`, `GET /orders` (+ `payment_status` / `delivery_status` / `search` / `per_page` filters), `GET /orders/{orderNumber}`, `GET /earnings`, `GET /subscription`. Controllers in `App\Http\Controllers\Reseller\`. `Order` reads lean on `BelongsToReseller` (`reseller.context` scopes them) — the order response is a deliberately narrow shape (mirrors `TrackOrderController`): the reseller sees their own margin (`reseller_profit`, `reseller_markup_pct`) but never `cost_price` / `standard_selling_price` / `platform_profit` or any supplier / payment-gateway field.
- **21 new tests** (`ResellerEarningsServiceTest` 7, `ResellerPortalReadTest` 10, `LedgerOwnerTypeTest` 4) — cross-tenant isolation on orders + ledger, admin-token rejection, internal-financial-field redaction. **Backend 1167/1167 fast + 10/10 concurrency**, Pint clean. No migration in 59a — `reseller_game` lands in 59c.
- **Local-env note:** the founder's local PHP has `memory_limit = 128M`; the full fast suite (1167 tests) now exhausts that and `php artisan test` OOMs mid-run (it re-execs a fresh PHP, so `php -d memory_limit=…` on the wrapper does not take). Run `php -d memory_limit=1024M vendor/bin/phpunit` locally. CI is unaffected (`shivammathur/setup-php` runs unlimited). Not a regression — reproduced on clean `staging`.

**Build addendum — 59b shipped 2026-08-31** (`feature/adr-059b-reseller-portal-app`). The `reseller/` Next.js app + the four read-only screens. No write surface (59c).

- **Third Next.js app, `reseller/`** — Next 16.3 / React 19 / Tailwind 4 / PrimeReact-Tailwind, `output: "standalone"`, dev server pinned to **`:3002`** (matches `config/services.php`'s `reseller_portal.url` default). `reseller/CLAUDE.md` → `@AGENTS.md`; `AGENTS.md` carries the standard `next dev` version-warning block plus a portal-specific note. Added to `scripts/dev.sh`.
- **Auth / session plumbing mirrors `admin/` exactly** (ADR-009): `lib/api-client.ts` copied verbatim; `lib/session.ts` + `lib/auth.ts` are the same shape with reseller-specific storage keys (`kerox_reseller_session`) and a `ResellerSessionPayload`; `hooks/useClientSession.ts` is the same `useSyncExternalStore` shape that dodges the `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` trap (ADR-038 decision 8); `app/api/login` + `app/api/logout` Route Handlers proxy to `/api/reseller/{login,logout}` and set/clear the presence-only httpOnly gate cookie (`kerox_reseller_session`); `proxy.ts` is the optimistic redirect (never a security boundary). `globals.css` + `components/prime-provider.tsx` + `context/ThemeContext.tsx` copied from `admin/` (shared design system).
- **Shell** — `components/PortalShell.tsx`: a lean fixed sidebar (Dashboard / Orders / Earnings / Subscription — six items when 59c adds Storefront + Withdrawal) + a header with the reseller's business name, a light/dark toggle, and sign-out. Deliberately not the full `admin/` TailAdmin collapsible-sidebar machinery — the portal is small and read-only.
- **Screens** (`app/(portal)/…`, all client components fetching with the bearer token): **Dashboard** (earnings/sales stat cards + subscription strip), **Orders** (filterable + paginated table → **Order detail** by `order_number`, showing the reseller's own margin but nothing internal), **Earnings** (withdrawable balance + paginated ledger — margin credits green, fee/withdrawal debits red), **Subscription** (tier snapshot + `reseller_tier_fee` charge history). Effects avoid synchronous `setState` (the lint rule the codebase enforces — `.then()`/`.finally()` chains + a `cancelled` flag; page-change spinners toggled in the click handler).
- **`tsc` / `eslint` / `next build` all clean.** No automated frontend tests (the repo has none for `admin/`/`storefront/` either — E2E golden-paths are the ADR-023 coverage).
- **CORS fix (same PR).** `config/cors.php`'s `allowed_origins` only listed `ADMIN_URL` + `STOREFRONT_URL`, so every `/api/reseller/*` browser read failed as a generic "Could not load" — the exact wall `storefront/` hit once before. Added `RESELLER_PORTAL_URL` (default `http://localhost:3002`) + a `CorsConfigTest` regression guard over all three origins. Found live-testing the portal in Chrome.
- **Live-verified in Chrome, 2026-08-31** (real Herd backend, seeded test reseller): login → all four screens render real data (dashboard tiles, orders list + delivery-status filter + order detail, earnings ledger with signed amounts, subscription snapshot + charge history), dark-mode toggle, sign-out → `/login`, and the post-logout `proxy.ts` gate all work. The only bug found was the CORS gap above, fixed in the same PR.
- **Deferred to 59c:** the impersonation banner (needs the per-request admin-tagging backend from ADR-058's deferral), all write screens, the `reseller_game` catalog toggle. **Deferred to ADR-060:** the Domain screen.

**Build addendum — 59c shipped 2026-08-31** (`feature/adr-059c-reseller-withdrawal-impersonation`). The re-scoped 59c: **Withdrawal + Profile + Impersonation**. (Storefront-config editors + Domain moved to ADR-060 — see the 59c re-scope note above.)

- **Migrations (2).** `resellers` += `bank_name` / `bank_account_no` / `bank_account_holder` (nullable) — a reseller stores its payout account once and the withdrawal form prefills from it. `withdrawals.requested_by` → **nullable** + a new nullable `reseller_user_id` FK: a reseller-originated withdrawal has no `admin_users` requester, and leaving `requested_by = null` means the admin approve step's maker-checker check (`$admin->id === $withdrawal->requested_by`) can never false-positive against a `reseller_user` id.
- **`Reseller\WithdrawalController`** (`index` / `store`) — the WTH-1..5 **request** side. `owner_type = 'reseller'`, `owner_id = <reseller id>`; balance checked via `ResellerEarningsService`; bank fields fall back to the saved profile; one open (pending/approved) request at a time. `store()` calls `LedgerService::openAccount('reseller', id)` — a reseller can have an earnings balance purely from `credit()` (order margin) with no `ledger_accounts` row, and the admin approve step's `withdraw()` does `firstOrFail()` on that row (same defensive open as `ResellerTierFeeService`). **Approval / rejection / completion stay on the unchanged admin flow.**
- **`Reseller\ProfileController`** (`show` / `update`) — the reseller edits only `contact_name` / `phone` / the three bank fields; `business_name` / `email` are admin-controlled and not accepted.
- **Impersonation portal side.** `/api/reseller/me` now returns an `impersonation` block (`session_id`, `admin_name`, `started_at`) — non-null only when an open `ResellerImpersonationSession` row exists for the exact token id (keyed on the session row, not the token's ability list, since a normal `['*']` login token technically `can()` anything). `POST /api/reseller/impersonation/end` (`Reseller\ImpersonationController`) closes that session + revokes the token — the portal "Exit" without switching to `/admin`.
- **Portal screens** — **Withdrawal** (request form prefilled from Profile, editable per-request; history table), **Profile** (read-only company block + editable contact/payout form). `app/impersonate` entry page reads the token from the URL **hash** (never a query string — stays out of server logs and Referer), POSTs it to `app/api/impersonate` (verifies via backend `/me`, sets the gate cookie), stores the session with `impersonating: true`, redirects to `/dashboard`. `ImpersonationBanner` renders above every screen from `PortalShell` when `session.impersonating`. Nav → 6 items (+ Withdrawal, + Profile). `/impersonate` excluded from the `proxy.ts` matcher (an entry point like `/login`).
- **Admin side.** `ResellerDetailModal` — on RES-4 impersonate success now `window.open(`${portal_url}/impersonate#token=…`, "_blank", "noopener")` instead of just printing a status string (which never even included the token).
- **13 new tests** (`ResellerProfileTest` 3, `ResellerWithdrawalTest` 6, `ResellerImpersonationPortalTest` 4) — including a portal-request-→-admin-approve integration that proves the ledger debit and the maker-checker no-false-positive. **Backend 1182/1182 fast + 10/10 concurrency**, Pint clean; `reseller/` + `admin/` `tsc` / `eslint` / `build` clean.
- **Live-verified in Chrome, 2026-08-31** (real Herd backend, seeded test reseller): Withdrawal request → `Withdrawal` row (`owner_type=reseller`, `requested_by=null`, `reseller_user_id` set, bank from form) + `ledger_accounts` row created + one-open-request UI guard; Profile edit → saved, `business_name` untouched; `/impersonate#token=` → banner "Impersonating {reseller} — acting as {admin}" → Exit → session closed (`ended_reason=manual`) + token revoked + redirect to `/login` (no cookie-vs-storage redirect loop).

**Deploy addendum — 2026-09-02.** The whole `reseller/` app (59a/b/c) is **live in production** as the `pekangame-reseller` Vercel project at **`reseller.pekangame.space`** — see [ADR-066](#adr-066-production-deploy-via-laravel-forge--reverses-adr-020s-docker-compose-containerisation)'s cutover addendum. `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL=https://api.pekangame.space`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIMEUI_LICENSE_KEY` set. Realtime pieces that depend on Reverb are inert (Reverb deferred at launch) but the portal has no Reverb dependency.

## ADR-060: Multi-tenant branded storefront + custom-domain infrastructure (Cloudflare for SaaS)

**Status:** Accepted (design) — 2026-08-30 (grilled with the founder via `/mattpocock-skills:grilling`, same session as ADR-056). ~~Blocked on `ADR-020` production deployment + `ADR-037` staging infra.~~ **Unblocked 2026-09-02 — production is live on Laravel Forge ([ADR-066](#adr-066-production-deploy-via-laravel-forge--reverses-adr-020s-docker-compose-containerisation)).** ~~This is now the next reseller build.~~ **2026-09-05: fully grilled (logo/hero-slides/domain-transfer-timing all resolved, see the addendum below); sequenced after the Cloudflare DNS transfer + real-client-IP fix so this ADR's custom-hostname code lands on clean infra. 2026-09-06: that Cloudflare cutover is DONE + verified ([ADR-020](#adr-020-production-host--digitalocean-basic-droplet--managed-mysql-docker-compose-cloudflare-fronted-phase-1-built-2026-07-30--deploy-mechanism-superseded-by-adr-066)'s "Cutover executed" section — NS on Cloudflare, `api` proxied with Origin CA + Full (Strict) + Authenticated Origin Pulls, origin locked, `trustProxies` fix in prod). This ADR is now fully unblocked and is the next reseller build.** Verification against production + local `Host` mocking (no deployed staging env exists, `ADR-037` is branch-workflow only) plus one real domain the founder has set aside specifically for end-to-end custom-hostname/SSL verification. **2026-09-06: Cloudflare cutover done ([ADR-020](#adr-020-production-host--digitalocean-basic-droplet--managed-mysql-docker-compose-cloudflare-fronted-phase-1-built-2026-07-30--deploy-mechanism-superseded-by-adr-066)) — this ADR is unblocked and is the next build. Same session, a scoped domain-lifecycle grill reversed decision 3 (Cloudflare for SaaS → Vercel-native custom domains) and fully pinned the `affiliate_domains` schema, the self-serve onboarding flow, provider opacity in the portal, and every CF/provider hostname lifecycle transition — see the "domain lifecycle fully specified" build addendum below, which also carries the 6-PR build split.**

**Context:**
- `ADR-020` / `ADR-066`: production is a DigitalOcean droplet managed by **Laravel Forge** (native PHP-FPM/nginx/Redis/Horizon), TLS via Forge Let's Encrypt, at `api.pekangame.space`; the three frontends are on Vercel. The Cloudflare-fronting / Cloudflare-for-SaaS piece (ADR-020 decision 8) is still pending the domain transfer. `ADR-037` staging *infra* (a deployed staging environment, as opposed to the branch workflow) is not built.
- Founder decision this session: **custom domains only, no subdomains.** A reseller buys their own domain and points it at the platform; the platform serves them a branded storefront on that domain. No `reseller.ourplatform.com` option.
- Money flow, settled this session: the end customer on a reseller's branded storefront pays the **full retail price into the one company CHIP account**. On payment + delivery, the ledger splits — platform revenue = the reseller's wholesale cost (`cost_price × (1 + tier.markup_percent)`, ADR-056); the reseller's earnings account is credited the margin (`customer_price − wholesale_cost`). The reseller never collects retail directly in this channel. `/admin/orders` shows every reseller order in full, labelled per reseller (founder).
- `storefront/` is one Next.js app on Vercel (`output: "standalone"` was removed in ADR-066 — Vercel-native, not Dockerized). `ADR-011`: guest checkout only, no cookies.

**Decision:**

1. **One `storefront/` app serves every reseller domain** — multi-tenant by `Host` header, resolved server-side (SSR / route handler) to a `Reseller` row via its `domains` JSON (existing column) or a dedicated `reseller_domains` table (decision 4). Not a deploy per reseller. The platform's own storefront is the `Reseller::platformOwner()` row on the platform's own domain — the same code path; `platformOwner` is just another tenant.

2. **Per-`Host` resolution scopes** branding (`reseller_branding` / `reseller_footer_settings` / `reseller_seo_settings`, `ADR-028` / `ADR-029`), catalog visibility (ADR-059 decision 3 game toggles), and pricing (ADR-056 — `customer_price = effective_base × (1 + reseller.markup_pct / 100)`). An unrecognized `Host` returns a generic 404 / landing — never the platform storefront's content under the wrong brand.

3. ~~**Custom-domain TLS via Cloudflare for SaaS (SSL for SaaS).** The reseller creates a CNAME (`shop.` or `www.` of their domain — an apex needs CNAME flattening, documented in the portal) pointing at a platform fallback-origin hostname; the platform registers their hostname via the Cloudflare Custom Hostnames API; Cloudflare issues and auto-renews the edge certificate. Chosen over host-Nginx Let's Encrypt automation because Cloudflare is already the platform's edge (`ADR-020` decision 8) and per-customer-domain cert lifecycle is precisely what this Cloudflare product does. Cost (~USD 0.10 / active hostname / month + plan) is accepted.~~ **Reversed 2026-09-06 — see the "domain lifecycle fully specified" build addendum below.** The premise (storefront is a Dockerised app on the droplet behind Cloudflare's edge) died with ADR-066 (storefront moved to Vercel) and the 2026-09-06 Cloudflare cutover (all three frontends deliberately kept Vercel-direct). Custom-domain TLS + routing is now Vercel's native per-project custom-domain support.

4. **Domain lifecycle** — the admin adds the reseller's domain in Reseller Management (ADR-058); the system calls the Cloudflare API to create the custom hostname, stores its status, and the portal's Domain screen (ADR-059) shows the reseller the CNAME + any DCV TXT record to set. Status polls Cloudflare (or consumes a Cloudflare webhook): `pending` → `active`. Reuses the `last_checked_at` / `last_status` shape from `PlayerValidatorProfile`. Deactivating (RES-5) or deleting (RES-6) a reseller removes the Cloudflare custom hostname.

5. **The ledger split is written at the same point the platform storefront writes its order ledger entries today** — on payment confirmed + delivery, inside the existing fulfillment path, extended to: (a) credit the reseller earnings account the margin, (b) book platform revenue at the wholesale amount rather than the full retail. `pricing_basis` (already on `orders`, `ADR-027`) gains a `reseller` value alongside `standard` / `member`; `reseller_id`, `reseller_markup_pct`, `reseller_profit` (columns already on `orders`) are snapshotted per ORD-9.

6. **No membership and no vouchers on a reseller storefront** — membership per `ADR-027` decision 9; vouchers deferred because "which ledger absorbs a voucher on a reseller sale" is an unanswered question and not needed for launch. The CHIP transaction fee is charged on top of the customer price, customer-borne, same as the platform storefront today (`transaction_fee`, ORD-9). Order delivery failure ⇒ retry (`ADR-004`); no voucher path on this channel for now.

7. **Reverb / realtime** (`ADR-047`) — the branded storefront's order-status tracker needs the same realtime channel wiring as the platform storefront; the per-`Host` origin must still reach `/app/` on the same backend. Confirm the Cloudflare custom-hostname config proxies WebSocket for reseller domains too.

**Rationale:** One app, `Host`-resolved (decision 1), is the only tenant model that doesn't multiply deploy / ops cost per reseller and keeps the platform storefront on the exact same code path (it's just `platformOwner`'s tenant). Cloudflare for SaaS (decision 3) is chosen not on cost but on fit — the alternative (Let's Encrypt on the host Nginx, on-demand issuance + renewal + LE rate-limit management for arbitrary customer domains) is a real ops burden for a solo founder, and Cloudflare is already the edge. Decision 5 (collect retail centrally, split in the ledger) is the founder's explicit money model and is what makes xenPlatform unnecessary (ADR-059 decision 6) — the ledger does the split.

Those are moved here, because they configure the per-`Host` branded storefront **this** ADR builds — before it exists, they'd edit a display that doesn't render. This ADR now also owns:
- **The `reseller_game` (or `reseller_disabled_games`) table + the portal Catalog screen** (decision 2's "ADR-059 decision 3 game toggles" — the table lands here now, using `BelongsToReseller` from creation).
- **The portal branding editor** — store name / description / support email+phone / social links on `reseller_branding`, **plus GA / FB / TikTok pixel IDs on `reseller_seo_settings`** (founder 2026-08-31: pixel IDs are the *only* SEO field a reseller controls; meta title/description templates, OG image, and schema toggles stay admin-authored and use `{store_name}` substitution). Footer text + legal pages (`terms_content` / `privacy_content` / `about_us_content`) + `footer_game_ids` stay **admin-only** — this **supersedes the part of `ADR-028` / `ADR-029` that anticipated a reseller editing its own footer/legal rows**; every brand renders the primary's footer with `{store_name}` substituted.
- **The `markup_pct` editor + live `PricingService::calculateForReseller()` preview** (ADR-059 decision 4) — lands with the checkout wiring in decision 5, so preview and charge share one path.
- **The Domain screen** (decision 4) — Cloudflare custom-hostname status + the CNAME / DCV records for the reseller to set.

This ADR's code PR is unblocked.** `storefront/` no longer builds with `output: "standalone"` (removed in ADR-066 — Vercel doesn't use it), so decision 1's "one Dockerized `storefront/` app" is now "one Vercel `storefront/` project" — the `Host`-resolution logic is identical, only the hosting shape changed.

Portal still recommends `www.` / `shop.` first (keeps the provider hidden — see the addendum's provider-opacity rule); apex-with-ALIAS/flattening points at the same hidden alias; only apex-without-ALIAS falls back to the raw A record.**

- `ADR-013`'s "every Order's `reseller_id` references the platform-owner row in MVP" stops being true here — the first non-platform-owner `reseller_id` orders appear. Update `ADR-013`'s status note.

**Prerequisites from the 2026-08-30 post-ADR-057 code review** (record here so they aren't rediscovered mid-build):
- **Extract a `PricingResolution` value object / resolver before wiring reseller pricing into checkout.** `CheckoutService::initiate()` currently selects `sellingPrice` / `platformProfit` / `resellerProfit` with inline `standard`-vs-`member` ternaries (lines ~67–77 + the `Order::create` array). Adding the `reseller-tier`-vs-`reseller-lapsed` branch on top makes that a 2×2 the ternary style won't hold. A resolver returning `(sellingPrice, platformProfit, resellerProfit, basis)` for all four cases keeps `initiate()` a consumer, not a decision tree.
- **`PricingService::calculateForReseller()` has no production caller yet — only unit tests.** This ADR is where it gets wired. "Done" requires an end-to-end proof (checkout → payment confirmed → `OrderFulfillmentService::creditProfit()` books platform revenue at the wholesale amount and credits the reseller earnings account the margin), not just the existing pricing-math unit tests.
- **`LedgerOwnerType` enum** — see ADR-059's consequence note. Do it in ADR-059 if that PR writes `ResellerEarningsService` first; otherwise here.
- **`DB::table('orders' | 'redirects' | 'reseller_*')` grep** in any `Host`-resolved or reseller-guard code path — these bypass `ResellerScope`. The per-`Host` storefront resolution (decision 1/2) runs guest (no reseller guard), so the scope doesn't fire there anyway — resolution must filter `reseller_id` / `Host` explicitly and must be tested for cross-tenant bleed directly, not assumed covered by the trait.

**Build addendum — open questions resolved, grilled 2026-09-05.** Every question this ADR's own text deliberately left open is now settled; combined with the Cloudflare-cutover sequencing above, this ADR is fully specified and ready to build once that cutover lands.

1. **Logo upload** — new `logo_url` (string, nullable) column on `affiliate_branding`. Portal self-serve (the affiliate uploads directly, same screen as the rest of the branding editor this ADR's earlier addendum already gave the portal — store name/description/contact/social links) — a dedicated small upload endpoint stores the file on the `public` disk under `affiliate-logos/{affiliate_id}.{ext}` and saves the resulting URL, deliberately not routed through the untenanted `gallery_images` table (no FK/tenant-scoping exists there today, and adding one just for this is more machinery than a single-column upload needs).
2. **Hero slides — per-affiliate, self-serve** (reversed from this addendum's own first recommendation during grilling, founder's explicit call): `hero_slides.affiliate_id` (nullable FK, `BelongsToAffiliate` — null = falls back to the primary/global slides, same "null = global" convention `membership_plans` already established) — **not** admin-only. The affiliate portal gets a self-serve hero-slide editor (reuses `/admin/hero-banner`'s existing shape: eyebrow/title/description/image/CTA/`is_active`/`sort_order`), the same self-serve posture as the rest of this ADR's storefront-config editors. This is a narrower reversal than it looks: footer/legal content (decision in the earlier addendum) stays admin-only because it's legally load-bearing text; a hero banner is marketing creative, squarely the kind of thing an affiliate should control themselves, same as their own logo (decision 1).
3. **Lapsed-tier storefront behavior, a real gap this grill surfaced** (not previously specified anywhere, including the "reseller-tier vs reseller-lapsed" 2×2 the prerequisites section already named but never resolved): a `Host`-resolved affiliate whose tier subscription has lapsed **keeps serving its storefront**, at **standard (non-wholesale) pricing** — no markup discount applied, `pricing_basis = 'standard'` for that brand's orders during the lapsed window, never a 404/503/"store unavailable" state. This is the natural product of the `PricingResolution` resolver the prerequisites section already calls for (decision: the lapsed branch of that 2×2 resolves to the same pricing path a brand-less guest order would use) — no new mechanism, just confirms which of the resolver's four branches "lapsed" actually maps to. Business rationale: the platform keeps selling (at full retail-equivalent margin) rather than taking a real domain offline over an unpaid tier fee; RES-5's existing deactivate-path (503 + Cloudflare hostname suspended) remains the actual "shut this affiliate down" lever, reserved for admin action, not automatic on a lapsed tier.
4. **Verification domain** — the founder has one real domain set aside specifically to verify the custom-hostname/Cloudflare/SSL flow end-to-end once both the cutover (ADR-020 addendum above) and this ADR's own build are done; not needed for logic-level verification (production + local `Host` mocking covers that, per the updated Status line).

Pure build from here, once the Cloudflare cutover lands — no further grilling needed.

**Build addendum — domain lifecycle fully specified + custom-domain mechanism reversed (Cloudflare for SaaS → Vercel-native), grilled 2026-09-06.** A scoped grill (domain-lifecycle sub-area only — the ledger split, the `PricingResolution` resolver, and `Host` resolution were explicitly *not* re-opened) closed every remaining unknown in how an affiliate's custom domain gets registered, verified, served, and torn down. The `affiliates.domains` JSON column and decision 3's Cloudflare-for-SaaS mechanism are both replaced.

**A. Data model — new `affiliate_domains` table, not `affiliates.domains` JSON.** The reference UI the founder wants (multiple domains, per-row validate tick, per-row status, a "Set Primary" button) needs per-row lifecycle state a JSON blob can't index or uniquely-constrain. Columns: `affiliate_id` (FK, `BelongsToAffiliate` trait like `Redirect`), `hostname` (**globally unique** — one hostname belongs to exactly one affiliate across the whole system), `is_primary` (bool), `status` (`pending` / `active` / `failed` / `suspended`), `provider` (string, default `'vercel'` — a provider-neutral column so a future swap needs no migration), `provider_ref` (nullable — the provider's domain-on-project identifier; **NULL on the seeded primary rows**), `verification` (JSON nullable — the TXT-challenge payload when the provider requires an ownership proof), `last_checked_at`, `verified_at`, `last_error` (nullable, sanitised), timestamps. The existing `affiliates.domains` JSON column is migrated to rows (prod has none) and dropped; `domains` is removed from `StoreAffiliateRequest` / `UpdateAffiliateRequest` (admin no longer sets domains — see F).

**B. Custom-domain TLS + routing — reverses decision 3, now Vercel-native.** One `storefront/` Vercel project, many attached custom domains (Pro: effectively unlimited, soft cap 100k/project, **$0 per domain** vs Cloudflare's ~$0.10/hostname/mo). A `VercelDomainService` (the one seam, credentials per ADR-046: `services.vercel.{token, team_id, storefront_project_id}`, token scoped to Domains on that project only) calls `projectsAddProjectDomain` / `projectsGetProjectDomain` / `projectsVerifyProjectDomain` / `projectsRemoveProjectDomain`. Vercel issues **and auto-renews** the per-domain certificate — no fallback-origin hostname, no DCV-delegation record, no Cloudflare Custom Hostnames API, no webhook-HMAC (decision 7's WebSocket concern also dissolves — the storefront's realtime channel already runs against `api.pekangame.space`, unchanged). A TXT ownership record is required **only** in the rare case the hostname is already attached to another Vercel account; otherwise the affiliate sets one record and Vercel auto-verifies.

**C. Provider opacity — the portal never names the provider (founder's explicit call, risk reduction).** The affiliate-facing Domain screen — every label, help string, status badge, and error message — must be provider-agnostic. Concretely:
- The CNAME target the affiliate copies is **a platform-owned alias**, `connect.pekangame.space`, a DNS-only (grey) CNAME in the platform's own Cloudflare zone pointing at the storefront project's Vercel CNAME target. A chained CNAME (`shop.affiliatedomain.com` → `connect.pekangame.space` → Vercel) resolves and verifies fine — this is the standard white-label pattern; confirm during PR-5.
- Apex-with-ALIAS/flattening points at the same `connect.pekangame.space` (no IP exposed). Apex-without-ALIAS is the only case that falls back to the raw A record (`76.76.21.21`) — a minor, accepted provider signal an affiliate would have to actively look up; `www.` / `shop.` is the recommended path and keeps the provider fully hidden.
- Every error surfaced from the Vercel API is **sanitised** before it reaches the affiliate ("this domain is already registered elsewhere — contact support", not the raw provider string). The ADR and internal docs may name Vercel; the portal may not.

**D. Onboarding + approval — full self-serve, no admin gate.** The affiliate adds a hostname in the portal → the system calls the provider API immediately → the row sits `pending` → the storefront serves that brand **only** once `status = active`. There is no admin approval step: provider-side domain-control verification *is* the ownership proof (the cert never issues for a domain the affiliate can't set DNS on). Guards: a per-affiliate cap of **5** domains; `hostname` globally unique; a denylist rejecting `*.pekangame.space` and any `is_owned` affiliate's domains; FormRequest rejection of IPs, ports, paths, and malformed hostnames. Only `status = 'active'` affiliates may manage domains — a not-yet-activated (`pending`) affiliate sees "activate your account first"; a **lapsed-subscription** affiliate keeps full domain management (domain ≠ subscription; its storefront still serves, at standard pricing per the 2026-09-05 addendum §3); a **deactivated** (RES-5) affiliate's Domain screen is read-only.

**E. Multi-domain, canonical, redirects.** Up to 5 domains per affiliate; exactly one `is_primary` (must be `active`), used for the canonical URL (`<link rel="canonical">`, OG url, sitemap) — non-primary domains still serve the full storefront, not a redirect, but carry the canonical tag pointing at the primary to avoid duplicate-content penalties. The first domain to reach `active` auto-becomes primary; the affiliate can re-point primary later, only among `active` domains. `www`↔apex redirects: the affiliate may set both hostnames, and the system registers both on Vercel with the redirect configured there; which one is canonical is the affiliate's choice.

**F. Admin controls — read-only + two break-glass buttons.** The existing `AffiliateDetailModal` gains a "Domains" section: the hostname list with per-row status and `last_checked_at`, plus **"Force re-check"** (calls the provider) and **"Remove domain"** (deletes the provider domain + the row — for abuse or an affiliate request). **No add-domain form in admin** — the single write path is affiliate self-serve (or the founder via RES-4 impersonation). This narrows decision 4's "the admin adds the reseller's domain".

**G. CF/provider hostname lifecycle transitions.**
| Event | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Affiliate deactivated (RES-5) | Every domain row → `suspended`; the provider domain is left attached but the storefront returns 503 for a `suspended`/non-`active` Host. Reactivate → rows return to `active` (DNS still valid) or `pending`. |
| Affiliate deleted (RES-6, earnings = 0 only) | `VercelDomainService` removes every provider domain; rows soft-delete with the affiliate. |
| Stuck `pending` (affiliate never sets DNS) | After **14 days** the daily reconcile command removes the provider domain and marks the row `failed`; Plunk reminder emails on day 3 and day 7. The affiliate can re-add. |
| Affiliate removes the CNAME after `active` | The poll (or a provider webhook, if wired) flips the row to `failed`; the storefront returns 503 for that Host. If it was the primary and another `active` domain exists, primary auto-fails-over to it; if none, that brand's storefront is unreachable but checkout/orders on other channels are unaffected. |

**H. Status sync.** Primary mechanism: a daily `app:sync-affiliate-domain-status` command polls the provider for every non-`active` / non-`suspended` row (same posture as the Digiflazz poll backstop). Plus a portal "Check now" button that polls on demand. A provider webhook is optional and additive, not required.

**I. Primary affiliate's own domains.** `pekangame.space` and `www.pekangame.space` are seeded as ordinary `affiliate_domains` rows on the primary affiliate (`provider_ref = NULL`, `status = 'active'`, `is_primary` on the apex). **All lifecycle logic — create / verify / suspend / delete / poll / stuck-pending TTL — skips any row where `provider_ref IS NULL`.** `Host` resolution treats them identically to any affiliate's rows, so there is exactly one code path. This matches ADR-061: the primary is just another tenant; "our own brand" and consumer-membership are the *only* real differentiators, and other `is_owned` brands (a second business) go through the normal Vercel custom-domain flow like any third party.

**J. Infra prerequisite (a `/wizard`-shaped founder step, before PR-5, not a code PR):** issue a Vercel API token (Domains scope, storefront project only) into Forge `.env`; create the `connect.pekangame.space` DNS-only CNAME in the platform Cloudflare zone pointing at the storefront project's Vercel CNAME target; confirm the storefront project's team is on the Vercel Pro plan.

**J — executed 2026-09-07 (founder-guided wizard, `adr-060-pr5-infra-wizard.sh`, not committed).** All seven stages done:

- **`services.vercel.*` credentials now in Forge `.env`** on the `api.pekangame.space` site (saved, **not deployed** — `config('services.vercel')` doesn't exist until PR-5 adds it, so the vars sit inert):

Value never entered the build chat; pasted straight into Forge.

The affiliate-facing CNAME target `connect.pekangame.space` is itself config too (`services.vercel.connect_cname` or similar) — not the raw Vercel target, which stays server-side.

**PR-5 is now unblocked.**

**PR-2 build addendum — `X-Storefront-Host` transport pinned, backend `Host` resolution shipped (2026-09-06).** One thing the ADR body never pinned: *how* the affiliate's domain reaches the backend. The storefront (Vercel) calls `api.pekangame.space` directly from both SSR and the browser, so the visitor's own domain (`shop.acme.com`) never arrives as the HTTP `Host` — it is `api.pekangame.space` on every backend call. Resolved: the storefront forwards it in an explicit **`X-Storefront-Host`** header (PR-3 wires the frontend side).

- **Trust model:** the header is spoofable, but a brand only controls branding display, catalog visibility, and markup — and a third-party affiliate's price is always ≥ the primary's (they add margin on top of standard retail), so there is no price arbitrage. Worst case is a mis-attributed `affiliate_id` on an order, which grieves an affiliate's margin for no attacker gain. A later hardening (signed header, or trusting only the Vercel egress) can tighten this without touching the resolver. **Founder-approved 2026-09-06.**
- **Shipped in PR-2:** `affiliate_domains` table (per addendum section A — globally-unique `hostname`, `status`/`is_primary`/`provider`/`provider_ref`/`verification`/`last_checked_at`/`verified_at`/`last_error`; `BelongsToAffiliate`). *(PR-2 also seeded the primary's hostnames from `STOREFRONT_PRIMARY_HOSTS` into this table; PR-3 dropped that in favour of a config short-circuit — see the PR-3 addendum. The table now holds only non-primary brands' domains.)* `AffiliateDomainStatus` enum. `App\Support\StorefrontBrand` (scoped holder, lazy `Affiliate::primary()` fallback). `App\Http\Middleware\ResolveStorefrontBrand` (`storefront.brand` alias) — reads the header, resolves an **active** row whose affiliate is **active + not soft-deleted**, else `abort(404)` (decision 2 — never serve a brand under an unknown/suspended host); clears the holder at the top of every request (Octane / sequential-test safety, mirrors `SetAffiliateContext`). Applied to the `catalog` route group + the membership routes. `BrandingController::show`, `SeoController` (settings/redirects/recordRedirectHit/scripts), `MembershipController`, `MembershipOtpController` resolve via `StorefrontBrand` instead of `Affiliate::primary()`.
- **Deliberately NOT in PR-2** (kept on `Affiliate::primary()`): all checkout/voucher-preview/catalog **pricing** and the catalog **cache keys** — those move per-brand atomically in PR-4 (pricing) / PR-3 (catalog display + cache), so display and charge never diverge in the gap. `BrandingController::legal` and `SeoController::robots` stay on the primary (legal text + crawler rules are admin-central per the earlier addendum). PR-2 is **entirely inert in production until PR-3 sends the header** — its value is the proven seam.
- **`.env.example`** owes a `STOREFRONT_PRIMARY_HOSTS=` line (the file is outside the agent's write scope — same standing gap as `RESELLER_PORTAL_URL` in ADR-058).

**PR-3 build addendum — storefront sends the header; primary hostnames are config not rows (2026-09-06).**

- **`X-Storefront-Host` from the frontend** (`storefront/src/lib/api-client.ts`): browser → `window.location.host`; SSR → the incoming request's `x-forwarded-host ?? host` via a guarded dynamic `import("next/headers")` (kept out of the client bundle). Also appended as a `__brand` query param on **cached** SSR reads so Next's Data Cache keys per brand regardless of header-keying behaviour (the backend ignores `__brand`).
- **Multi-tenant ⇒ dynamic rendering.** Reading `headers()` opts every storefront route out of static prerendering (`ƒ Dynamic` in the build) — inherent to a per-`Host` shell, and it reverses part of ADR-071's static-shell posture. `next: { revalidate: 60 }` still Data-Caches the branding/SEO/catalog `fetch`es (independent of route-level dynamic), now per brand, so a warm render is cache-lookups not backend round-trips. `safeRead` + `resolveStorefrontHost` both call `unstable_rethrow` so the `headers()` prerender bail-out (and `notFound()`/`redirect()`) propagate cleanly instead of being swallowed and hanging `next build`.
- **Primary hostnames are `STOREFRONT_PRIMARY_HOSTS` config, not `affiliate_domains` rows** (revises PR-2 addendum section I). `ResolveStorefrontBrand` short-circuits a header matching `config('services.storefront.primary_hosts')` straight to `Affiliate::primary()` with no DB lookup; the table holds **only non-primary brands' domains**. This removes the local-dev / E2E migration-timing friction (just set the env, no seed-before-migrate). The PR-2 migration's seed block is dropped (it was a no-op in every environment — the env was set nowhere). "Our own infra hostnames are config; customer domains are data."
- **Per-brand NOW:** store name / description / support contacts, SEO meta + GA/FB/TikTok pixels, Organization JSON-LD, footer store name — all already flow from the PR-2 brand-resolved endpoints once the header arrives, so the frontend needed no render-layer changes beyond the header. **Deferred:** logo (`affiliate_branding.logo_url` → PR-6), per-brand hero slides (`hero_slides.affiliate_id` → PR-6), catalog + checkout **pricing** and the backend catalog **cache keys** (→ PR-4, atomically with the ledger split so display never diverges from charge). An unrecognised `Host` currently degrades to the fallback storefront (default branding, empty catalog) rather than a hard "store unavailable" page — the hard 404 needs a storefront `middleware.ts` and waits for PR-5, when custom domains (hence unknown hosts) first exist.
- **E2E:** `e2e/scripts/boot-backend.sh` exports `STOREFRONT_PRIMARY_HOSTS=localhost` (the Playwright storefront host).
- Production impact: the live `pekangame.space` storefront now routes through the header path but resolves (via the config short-circuit) to the same `Affiliate::primary()` — **zero behaviour change**, only the render mode shifts to dynamic.

**Build addendum — PR-4 grilled + re-split into four sub-PRs, foundation-first (2026-09-06).** A full codebase audit of every money seam ahead of PR-4, then a `/mattpocock-skills:grilling` session with the founder. The founder's framing drove it: **affiliate / reseller-wallet / membership are one ecosystem, serviced differently — the backend core must be solid before a fourth money path is wired onto it.** The audit found the "one seam" is only half-built: `CheckoutPricingResolver` covers storefront checkout (standard/member) but the reseller-wallet channel (API + Bot) hand-rolls the same `PricingService::calculateForAffiliate(cost, standard, tier%, 0.0)` call **inline in three places** (`ResellerOrderPlacementService`, `ResellerBotService::handleListGamePackages`, `ResellerApi/CatalogController`), and `Order::query()->create([...])` is hand-built in three services with divergent column sets and duplicated idempotency/dispatch logic. Wiring `affiliate` pricing into that as-is would deepen the divergence at the exact moment real third-party money starts splitting.

**Decisions:**

1. **`PricingResolution` becomes the cross-channel money VO for product-sale order channels** (guest top-up / member top-up / affiliate storefront / reseller-wallet). `CheckoutPricingResolver` is renamed **`OrderPricingResolver`** with two channel-explicit entry methods, each returning one `PricingResolution`:
   - `resolveStorefront(...)` — the existing standard/member/affiliate/affiliate-lapsed 2×2 (`tierMarkupPct` null ⇒ Standard basis, non-null ⇒ Affiliate basis).
   - `resolveResellerWallet(costSen, standardSellingSen, tierMarkupPct)` — the wallet channel, mirroring `PricingService`'s own `calculate()` vs `calculateForAffiliate()` split.
   `ResellerOrderPlacementService`, `ResellerBotService` and `ResellerApi/CatalogController` all call `resolveResellerWallet()` — the three inline copies are deleted.
   **Membership subscription stays a parallel path and is out of scope** — it is a subscription *fee* (`MembershipCheckoutAttempt`, `membership_fee` ledger credit), not a product sale; it shares only `LedgerService` + the payment gateway + `CheckoutTotalService`, never `Order` / `PricingResolution` / fulfilment. That is correct and deliberate — "one ecosystem" for membership means one *ledger*, not one order path.

2. **New `OrderFactory` seam** (`OrderFactory::create(OrderDraft): Order`) — the single place the money-critical `Order::query()->create([...])` array is built and the unique-constraint (`23000`) violation is caught (→ `DuplicateOrderException`). `OrderDraft` is a DTO carrying a `PricingResolution` plus every non-pricing field. Deliberately **does not** own the payment leg or `FulfillOrderJob::dispatch` — the storefront flow (create → maybe gateway → Pending) and the wallet flow (create → debit → Paid → fulfil) are genuinely different orchestrations and stay in their own services. `SandboxOrderController`'s hand-rolled create is left for a later pass (it is `is_test`-only, super-admin-only, and already drifted from the current schema).

3. **Storefront-brand resolution gates on `pricing_basis` / `is_owned`, never on primary-ness.** An `is_owned` brand (the founder expects 2–3: e.g. a KOL who takes a flat monthly payment *from* the platform rather than a per-order markup, so the platform takes 100% of the margin under that KOL's brand name) behaves with **full primary parity** — membership, vouchers, standard-chain pricing off its own `markup_pct`, `affiliate_profit` accruing to a company sub-account (ADR-061: every `is_owned` brand's ledger is company money). Only a genuine third-party `affiliate`-basis order is treated differently. The platform→KOL monthly payout mechanism is **its own future ADR**, not PR-4.

4. **`orders.wholesale_markup_pct`** (nullable `decimal(5,2)`) — snapshot the wholesale tier markup actually applied, for the `affiliate` and `reseller-wallet` bases (ORD-9: snapshot every price input). Without it, `OrderResendService` cannot recompute profit correctly for those bases — a latent bug **already live** for `reseller-wallet` orders (its `resend()` routes every non-`member` basis through the standard `PricingService::calculate()`, silently wrong for a wallet order). PR-4b makes `OrderResendService` branch fully on `PricingBasis` via `OrderPricingResolver` with the order's frozen inputs, and supports resending a `reseller-wallet` order (not refund-only). Existing wallet-order rows are backfilled (`wholesale_markup_pct` derived from the stored `platform_profit + cost_price`, or the reseller's current tier — settled at build time).

5. **Vouchers become brand-scoped** — `vouchers.affiliate_id` **NOT NULL** (existing rows backfilled to `Affiliate::primary()`; production is not yet commercially live so this is near-empty). A voucher issued from Brand A is redeemable **only** on Brand A — the same "brand-scoped customer instrument" rule membership session tokens already follow (`session['affiliate_id'] !== $affiliateId`). `VoucherService::issue()` records the brand (compensation vouchers from `storeFromOrder` take `order.affiliate_id`); `preview()` / `redeem()` / `findUsableVoucher()` filter on it against the `Host`-resolved brand; the admin promo-voucher form gets a **required brand picker** (default primary); `merge()` gains a same-brand assertion alongside its existing same-customer one. The voucher *accounting* is unchanged and already reconciles — `VoucherService::issue()` books the full liability as a `voucher_issued` debit to **Platform** at creation, so **Platform always absorbs voucher cost, including on a third-party affiliate storefront** (this closes ADR-060 decision 6's "which ledger absorbs a voucher on a reseller sale" open question — Platform does, always; an affiliate-shares-the-discount model stays unbuilt until an affiliate actually asks).

6. **Grace ≠ Lapsed.** ADR-060's 2026-09-05 addendum §3 says a "lapsed" tier falls back to standard pricing — precisely, the fallback is `!AffiliateSubscriptionStatus::grantsWholesaleRate()`, which is **`Lapsed` or no subscription**. A subscription in `Grace` (missed a charge, still inside the 3-day window) **keeps wholesale-tier pricing** (ADR-056). `Affiliate::wholesaleTierMarkupPct(): ?float` is the one place this is resolved (`grantsWholesaleRate() ? tier.markup_percent : null`), consumed by catalog + checkout + preview + voucher-preview.

**PR re-split (supersedes the single "PR-4" line above):**

| PR | Scope | Prod effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **PR-4a** ✅ **merged (PR #120)** | `OrderFactory` + `OrderDraft` (decision 2) · `Affiliate::wholesaleTierMarkupPct()` (decision 6). `CheckoutService` + `ResellerOrderPlacementService` migrate onto `OrderFactory`. `OrderFactory` uses Laravel's `UniqueConstraintViolationException` not the callers' old SQLSTATE-`23000` string check (which also matched a NOT NULL violation). **The `Affiliate::primary()` `once()` memo was dropped** — no memo precedent in the codebase (`PlatformSettings::current()` re-queries every call), a process-global `once()` risks stale reads in a multi-request test, and PR-4c makes it moot: `CatalogController` switches to the request-scoped `StorefrontBrand` holder, which already memoizes `Affiliate::primary()` once per request. | None — pure refactor, suites green |

**Consequence to track:**

Left for the standing Reports restructure backlog, not PR-4; PR-4c's feature test only proves the *ledger* split, which `ReportService` reads from directly.

**PR-4c build addendum — per-brand pricing + ledger split wired (2026-09-06).** No new migration (`orders.wholesale_markup_pct` landed in PR-4b); the whole PR is seam-wiring.

- **Routes.** `storefront.brand` middleware added to `/checkout`, `/checkout/preview-totals`, `/vouchers/preview` (chained after each route's existing throttle). No header / a `primary_hosts` header → `Affiliate::primary()` (byte-identical to before); an unknown / suspended / deactivated host `abort(404)`s **before** any order is created.
- **Checkout.** `CheckoutController` injects `StorefrontBrand`, resolves `$affiliate = $this->storefrontBrand->get()` in both `store()` and `previewTotal()`, and passes `tierMarkupPct: $affiliate->wholesaleTierMarkupPct()` into `CheckoutRequest` / `CheckoutService::previewTotal()`. `affiliateId`, `affiliateMarkupPct`, and the membership gate/lookup already keyed off `$affiliate` — now the `Host`-resolved one. `OrderPricingResolver::resolveStorefront()` produces `PricingBasis::Affiliate` (+ `wholesaleMarkupPct`) when the tier is Active/Grace, `Standard` when lapsed/none — `OrderFactory` already snapshots all of it.
- **Ledger split.** Unchanged. `creditProfit()` books `order.platform_profit` → Platform and `order.affiliate_profit` → `LedgerOwnerType::Affiliate` at `owner_id = order.affiliate_id`. Because the order is now attributed to the resolved brand and the resolver computed `platform_profit = wholesale − cost` / `affiliate_profit = the affiliate's margin`, a real third-party sale splits to the affiliate's own account with zero fulfilment-path change.
- **Catalog.** `CatalogController` injects `StorefrontBrand`; `sellingPriceSen()` swaps `PricingService::calculate()` → `calculateForAffiliate($cost, $std, $brand->wholesaleTierMarkupPct(), $brand->markup_pct)` (null tier ⇒ byte-identical to the old call — the primary listing does not move a sen). Both cache keys gain `.brand.{id}`: `packagesCacheKey()` keeps its tag set (tag-flush still reaches every brand), the index key is looped-and-`forget()`ed per brand id (`Affiliate::withTrashed()->pluck('id')`) since the default `database` store has no tags. `forgetPackagesCache()` now delegates its index purge to `forgetIndexCache()`.
- **Voucher preview.** `VoucherPreviewController` resolves the brand and prices via `calculateForAffiliate()` — the discount preview is against the same price the real checkout charges. (Member pricing is still not applied here — a pre-existing gap, unchanged.)
- **Tests.** New `AffiliateStorefrontCheckoutTest` (5 — brand pricing + attribution, `previewTotal` == charge anti-divergence, lapsed-tier standard fallback, header-less = primary, unknown host 404s pre-order). `OrderFulfillmentServiceTest` +1 (affiliate credit lands on `owner_id = affiliate_id`). `CatalogControllerTest` +1 (per-brand `selling_price_sen`, header-less unchanged) — `test_index_survives_a_real_database_cache_round_trip` repointed to the brand key. `VoucherPreviewControllerTest` +1. **1527/1527 fast + 13/13 concurrency** (real MySQL), Pint clean.
- **Not in PR-4c:** Playwright stays primary-brand (a real per-brand custom domain needs PR-5's `VercelDomainService`); voucher brand-*scoping* (redeemable-only-on-issuing-brand) is PR-4d.

**PR-5 build addendum — custom-domain lifecycle (Vercel-native), built 2026-09-07.** Shipped as one PR (`feature/adr-060-pr-5-domains`) in four commits — a CI-tuning commit + 5a backend / 5b portal / 5c admin+storefront — to hold down the private-repo Actions-minute burn (~135 runs/7d) that fewer, larger PRs reduce. The CI commit is its own small addendum below.

- **The seam is an `AffiliateDomainProvider` interface**, not the concrete `VercelDomainService` the ADR body names — `VercelDomainProvider` for prod, `NullDomainProvider` bound whenever `services.vercel.{token,team_id,storefront_project_id}` is unset (local dev / CI / the fast + e2e suites run the whole lifecycle with **no network call**; a real custom-domain end-to-end is verified against production + the founder's reserved domain). `services.vercel.*` in `config/services.php` reads the vars the PR-5 infra wizard already parked in Forge `.env`; `connect_cname` (`connect.pekangame.space`) is the affiliate-facing CNAME target and the raw Vercel target never leaves the server.
- **`VercelDomainProvider`** → `POST /v10/projects/{id}/domains`, `GET`/`POST …/verify`/`DELETE /v9/…`; `?teamId=`. Every failure is re-thrown as a `DomainProviderException` with an **affiliate-safe, provider-un-named** message (`alreadyInUse` is the one specially-handled case); the raw Vercel error goes to the log only. `ConnectionException` → the same generic exception.
- **`AffiliateDomainService`** — the deep module and **single writer** of `affiliate_domains`. `add` (normalise + `assertHostnameAllowed` denylist [`*.pekangame.space`, `connect_cname`, `primary_hosts`] + 5-domain cap + global-unique `hostname` + provider attach with **row rollback on failure**), `recheck` (`pending→active` with auto-primary; `active→failed` on `missing` with **primary fail-over**), `remove`, `setPrimary` (active only), `suspendAll`/`resumeAll` (RES-5), `removeAllForDelete` (RES-6), `tearDownStuckPending`. Every provider-side step **skips a null-`provider_ref` row** (the primary's config-seeded hostnames).
- **Portal** — `/api/affiliate/domains` (index/store/recheck/primary/destroy) + `reseller/` **Domains** screen: CNAME instructions (provider never named), add form (disabled at cap / when the account is inactive), per-row status + hint + `last_error`, Check-now / Set-primary / Remove. A **lapsed subscription keeps full domain management** (domain ≠ subscription); a **deactivated** affiliate's screen is read-only (`assertWritable` 403).
- **Admin** — `AffiliateDetailModal` "Custom domains" section (list + **Force re-check** / **Remove**, no add path); RES-5 `updateStatus` suspends/resumes domains; RES-6 `destroy` tears them down at the provider **first** (a provider failure aborts the delete). The free-text `affiliates.domains` textarea + table column are gone.
- **`affiliates.domains` JSON column dropped** (`2026_09_07_040000`) — replaced by the `affiliate_domains` table in PR-2, last readers removed here. Ran against the local dev DB.
- **`app:sync-affiliate-domain-status`** daily (routes/console.php, same inert-until-real-cron pattern) — polls `pending`/`failed` provider-managed rows, tears down rows **stuck `pending` past 14 days** (`services.vercel.stuck_pending_days`), sends **day-3 / day-7** Plunk DNS reminders (best-effort; a missed cron day just skips that day's reminder — no `reminder_sent_at` column).
- **Storefront hard 404** — `proxy.ts` checks each `Host` against `GET /api/catalog/storefront-status` (cached per host, 60s) and **rewrites an unrecognised custom domain to a static `/store-unavailable` page** rather than the degraded fallback storefront; `ResolveStorefrontBrand`'s unknown-host 404 now carries `{code: "unknown_storefront_host"}` so the proxy can tell it from any other 404. A network blip keeps serving.

**Deviations from the 2026-09-06 addendum, recorded:**
- **RES-6 hard-deletes the domain rows** (addendum G says "soft-delete with the affiliate") — `AffiliateDomain` has no `SoftDeletes` and a hard delete frees the globally-unique `hostname` for re-use, which RES-6's earnings-zero precondition makes safe.
- The seam name (`AffiliateDomainProvider` interface, not `VercelDomainService`) — so the no-op local/CI binding is clean; the provider-neutral `provider` column already anticipated a swap.

**Tests:** `AffiliateDomainServiceTest` (16), `AffiliateDomainControllerTest` (7), `VercelDomainProviderTest` (6, `Http::fake`), `SyncAffiliateDomainStatusCommandTest` (4), `Admin\AffiliateControllerTest` +4, `ResolveStorefrontBrandTest` +2. Fast suite **1573 green**; admin + storefront + reseller tsc/eslint/build clean; Pint clean.

**Still open after PR-5:** PR-6 (portal storefront-config editors — branding / logo / hero slides / GA-FB-TikTok pixel / `markup_pct` + live preview / `affiliate_game` catalog toggle). `.env.example` still owes `STOREFRONT_PRIMARY_HOSTS=` + now `VERCEL_*` (outside agent write scope). Founder's real reserved domain = the e2e custom-hostname/SSL verification, once PR-6 lands.

**PR-6 build addendum — affiliate storefront-config editors, built 2026-09-07** (`feature/adr-060-pr-6-storefront-config`). The last piece of ADR-060 — the `reseller/` portal "Storefront" screen (four tabs) that writes the per-`Host` branded storefront PR-1…4d renders. Everything the planning addendum above pinned, built as designed; the deviations and build-time findings are recorded here.

- **Schema** (`2026_09_07_050000`, ran against the local dev DB): `affiliate_game` (`is_visible`, absent = visible), `hero_slides.affiliate_id` (nullable, null = global) + `hero_slides.image_path` (upload cleanup), `affiliate_branding.logo_path` (a disk path — **deviation from the 2026-09-05 addendum's `logo_url`/absolute-URL**; the `AffiliateBranding::logo_url` accessor derives the URL at read time from `config('filesystems.gallery_disk')`, so the future R2 cutover rewrites no rows), `affiliate_markup_changes` (append-only audit — **reversed from the planning-round "no audit table" position** per Q17).
- **`App\Services\Media\ImageIngestService`** — the shared logo + hero upload seam, backed by **`intervention/image` v3** (GD driver bound in `AppServiceProvider`). Re-encodes to WebP q82, caps the longest edge (logo 512 / hero 1600), `->orient()` applies + strips EXIF rotation, writes through `config('filesystems.gallery_disk')`. GD-only was the first plan and was reversed during the grill — the box's GD build being WebP-compiled is not guaranteed on Forge and EXIF-orientation is hand-rolled work GD does not do. `FormRequest` guards: `mimes:jpg,jpeg,png,webp` (SVG rejected — not rasterisable), `max:2048` KB, `dimensions:max_width=5000,max_height=5000` (bounds decoder memory).
- **Thin per-resource controllers under `Affiliate\Storefront\`** (`BrandingController` / `SeoController` / `HeroSlideController` / `StorefrontGameController` / `PricingController`), routed `/api/affiliate/storefront/*` inside the existing `auth:affiliate` + `account.type:affiliate` + `affiliate.context` group. `assertWritable` extracted to `Affiliate\Concerns\AssertsAffiliateWritable` (shared with `DomainController`); a lapsed subscription keeps full edit access, a deactivated (RES-5) affiliate is read-only.
  - **Tenant scoping is by hand** (`$request->user()->affiliateOwner()->id` + `withoutAffiliateScope()->where('affiliate_id', …)`), not the `BelongsToAffiliate` global scope — matching every other portal controller. Two reasons found building: (a) `SubstituteBindings` runs before `affiliate.context`, so a `{heroSlide}` route-model binding resolves before `CurrentAffiliate` is active (each by-id action gets an explicit `assertOwned` 404, same as `DomainController`); (b) the test kernel does not flush `scoped` singletons or the resolved guard user between sequential requests, so relying on the scope for isolation is fragile in tests too.
  - `BrandingController::show` aggregates `affiliate_branding` + the three pixel fields of `affiliate_seo_settings` so the Branding tab loads in one call; the two write paths stay split (`SeoController` owns the pixels). `update` drops blank `social_links` entries server-side.
  - **Pixel IDs** — `UpdateSeoRequest` charset-gates to `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]*$` (`max:64`): the value lands inside an inline `<script>` in the storefront `<head>` (`fbq('init', …)` / `ttq.load(…)`), so this is a stored-XSS gate, not a format check. The storefront `layout.tsx` additionally `JSON.stringify`s the id into those snippets rather than raw `'${id}'` interpolation (defence in depth). GA uses `<GoogleAnalytics gaId>` and was already safe.
  - **Hero slides** — cap 6, `is_active` toggle only (no schedule window), `primary_cta_label`/`primary_cta_href` **required** (the `hero_slides` columns are NOT NULL and a CTA-less banner is a dead slide). Multipart create; edit uses `_method=PUT` spoofing (PHP can't parse a multipart PUT body). The public `HeroSlideController::index()` is now `Host`-brand-aware — a brand's own `live()` slides, else the null-`affiliate_id` global set (fallback on *effective content*, not row existence); cache key `catalog.public.hero_slides.brand.{id}`. An admin write of a global slide busts every per-brand hero key (loop brand ids); an affiliate write busts only its own.
  - **`StorefrontGameController`** — `affiliate_game` upsert; min-1-visible-game guard (422 on the last one). `CatalogController::index()`/`show()`/`packages()` exclude a brand's `is_visible = false` games; `forgetIndexCache(?int $brandId)` gained a single-brand variant, a per-brand tag `catalog.packages.brand.{id}` was added to the packages cache, and `forgetCacheForBrand()` flushes just that brand.
  - **`PricingController`** — `markup_pct` write hard-capped at the admin-set `max_markup_pct` (422 over), floor 0, writes an `affiliate_markup_changes` row, flushes only this brand's catalog caches. `show` returns `effective_markup_pct = min(markup_pct, max_markup_pct)` (a stale higher value from a lowered ceiling never reaches a customer — the storefront resolver already clamps, this just surfaces it). `preview` prices 3 low/mid/high packages from the brand's visible catalog via `PricingService::calculateForAffiliate` (the same math as the real charge) with a `wholesale_rate_active` flag for the lapsed-subscription note.
- **Storefront (`storefront/`)** — `Branding` wire schema + `Logo` gain `logo_url`; `SiteHeader`/`SiteFooter` render the brand's uploaded logo (plain `<img>`, backend-hosted — a ~34px mark gains nothing from `next/image` and this sidesteps the per-brand `remotePatterns` question) and fall back to the placeholder mark. `SiteHeader`'s wordmark now follows `storeName` instead of a hardcoded "PEKANGAME" (still "PEKANGAME" for the primary).
- **Portal (`reseller/`)** — one "Storefront" nav item → `(portal)/storefront/page.tsx`, four lazy tabs, active tab in `?tab=` (seeded via a client-only lazy `useState`, no `useSearchParams` Suspense boundary). Hand-typed fetch layer in `lib/portal.ts` (the portal has no Zod); shared form primitives in `components/storefront/shared.tsx`; each tab degrades to read-only on the response `writable` flag. Markup preview is a debounced backend call rendering a card-per-package stack (mobile-first — ~80% of traffic).
- **R2 deferred** — every new upload routes through `config('filesystems.gallery_disk')` (local droplet disk today), so the future Cloudflare R2 ADR is a config + one-off data migration. WebP-at-upload ships now for these paths; gallery→WebP + the bucket cutover fold into that ADR ([[project_cloudflare_r2_storage_backlog]]).
- **Out of scope, unchanged:** theme/colour editor (future THM ADR), `is_owned` second-brand portal path (no such brand), Zod for the portal, retrofitting `assertWritable` onto `ProfileController`.

**Tests:** `Affiliate\Storefront\{Branding,HeroSlide,StorefrontGame,Pricing}ControllerTest` + `ImageIngestServiceTest` (25 new); `Admin\HeroSlideControllerTest` + the public `HeroSlideControllerTest` updated for the per-brand cache key + a seeded primary. Fast suite **1598 green**; `reseller/` + `storefront/` tsc/eslint/build clean; Pint clean. No concurrency suite (no money-critical locking) and no E2E golden-path change.

**Still open after PR-6:** `.env.example` owes `STOREFRONT_PRIMARY_HOSTS=` + `VERCEL_*` (outside agent write scope). Founder's real reserved domain = the end-to-end custom-hostname/SSL verification. A real PekanGame logo asset + hero artwork (the storefront placeholder mark is still in place). ADR-060 is otherwise **complete**.

**CI-minute tuning addendum (ADR-066), 2026-09-07.** Private repo, billed Actions minutes: ~135 workflow runs over 7 days was burning ~1900 min/mo, driven by run *count* (7 parallel jobs, each rounded up to the minute) not run size. Two `ci.yml` changes, both safe today because `staging`/`main` have **no branch protection or rulesets** (a skipped workflow can't wedge a never-reported required check):
- **`concurrency: { group: per-PR, cancel-in-progress: pull_request only }`** — a newer commit on a PR cancels the older in-flight run (double runs were visible in history). A `push:main` run is never cancelled (deploy must finish).
- **`pull_request.paths-ignore: ['docs/**', '**/*.md']`** — a docs-only PR no longer runs the full matrix; `push:main` stays unfiltered so a docs merge still fires `deploy` (a harmless no-op rebuild).

`cancel-in-progress` means a superseded commit never gets its own green check — acceptable. Revisit both if branch protection is ever turned on (would need the "skipped = success" dummy-job pattern or `dorny/paths-filter` in-job).
