**Build addendum — PR-G code shipped 2026-09-05** (`feature/adr-072-pr-g-reseller-portal`, depends on PR-A + PR-D, both merged). Everything the planning addendum above pinned, built as designed — several build-time judgment calls found while building, all documented below, no real deviation from the addendum's own decisions.

- **`affiliate_users` polymorphic migration** (`2026_09_05_040000_make_affiliate_users_owner_polymorphic`) — additive-then-drop, same discipline as every other polymorphic-owner rollout in this codebase: add nullable `owner_type`/`owner_id`, backfill every existing row `owner_type='affiliate'`/`owner_id=affiliate_id`, make both non-nullable, drop `affiliate_id` + its FK/index. **Gotcha found building it**: the drop had to use `dropForeign(['affiliate_id'])` (the array-of-columns form), not `dropForeign('affiliate_users_affiliate_id_foreign')` (the explicit-name string form) — SQLite's schema grammar (the fast test suite's driver) throws "This database driver does not support dropping foreign keys by name" on the string form; PR-A's own rename migration already established this array-form convention for exactly this reason, re-confirmed here. Local dev DB (sqlite) migrated clean via plain `migrate`, zero existing `affiliate_users` rows to backfill (still unseeded beyond the founder's own primary Affiliate portal users, per the local-dev-DB note — none created yet).
- **Build-time judgment call — `AffiliateUser::owner()` resolved via two explicit accessor methods (`affiliateOwner()`/`resellerOwner()`), not Eloquent `morphTo()`/`morphMap()`.** Confirmed by grep before writing any code: this codebase has never used Eloquent's polymorphic relations anywhere — `LedgerEntry`/`LedgerAccount`'s own `owner_type`/`owner_id` pair (`LedgerOwnerType`) is read back manually by every caller, never via a relation. A new `App\Services\Auth\AccountOwnerType` enum (`affiliate`/`reseller`, with the same `coerce()` idiom `LedgerOwnerType` established) types the column; `Affiliate::users()`/`Reseller::users()` are scoped `hasMany`s (`->where('owner_type', ...)`) rather than `morphMany()`, for the same consistency reason. `AffiliateUser::ownerBusinessName()` is the one place both branches fold into a single call for `AffiliateInviteService` to use.
- **`EnsureAccountType`** (`app/Http/Middleware`, alias `account.type`, parameterized) — the decision-4 gate. Applied to every existing Affiliate-portal route (`account.type:affiliate`, paired with `affiliate.context` — `/logout` and `/me` stay outside both, shared by both account types per decision 6) and every new `/api/reseller-portal/*` route (`account.type:reseller`). **`SetAffiliateContext` itself also hardened** to 403 a `reseller`-owned account outright rather than silently no-op-activating ADR-057's tenant scope for it — a second, independent check specific to that one middleware, defense-in-depth alongside `EnsureAccountType` being the primary gate.
- **`wallet_topup_attempts`** (`reseller_id` FK cascade, unique `reference`, `amount_sen`, `status`, `chip_payment_ref` nullable, timestamps — per the task spec) **plus three build-time-necessary additions**: `total_charged_sen` (the fee-inclusive CHIP charge amount — decision 3's "CHIP's transaction fee added on top and borne by the reseller" is meaningless without somewhere to store the two different numbers, mirrors `membership_checkout_attempts.fee_sen`/`total_charged_sen`), `channel_code` (needed by the reconcile command to resolve which gateway to ask, mirrors the same column on `membership_checkout_attempts`), and `checkout_url` (the portal has to redirect the reseller somewhere to actually pay — mirrors the same column there too). `WalletTopupAttemptStatus` enum, `App\Models\WalletTopupAttempt`.
- **`App\Services\Reseller\ResellerWalletTopupService::initiate()`** — decision 3's self-serve flow, mirrors `MembershipSubscriptionService::initiate()`'s shape (one synchronous CHIP call on the customer path, server-computed amount). Decision 8's "one pending attempt" guard locks this reseller's own `('reseller_wallet', id)` `ledger_accounts` mutex row (the exact same row `LedgerService::debit()` already locks for this reseller's balance) inside the transaction that checks-then-creates the attempt row — proven by a real second-process concurrency test (`ResellerWalletTopupConcurrencyTest` + its `app:reseller-wallet-topup-test-initiate` console helper, same subprocess shape as `ResellerOrderPlacementConcurrencyTest`), not just a unit assertion. `ResellerWalletService::completeTopup()` is the idempotent credit-and-mark-paid seam `ChipWebhookController`'s new third branch and `ReconcilePendingWalletTopupsCommand` both call.
- **`ChipWebhookController`** gained the third fallback branch exactly as decision 11 specifies, mirroring the Order/Membership branches' own dedupe/amount-check/acknowledge shape.
- **`ReconcilePendingWalletTopupsCommand`** — mirrors `ReconcilePendingPaymentsCommand`'s shape (per the task's own instruction), not `ReconcilePendingMembershipPaymentsCommand`'s. **Build-time judgment call**: scheduled every 15 minutes (`services.wallet_topup_reconciliation.pending_after_minutes`, default 5), not daily like the membership reconcile command — a `WalletTopupAttempt`'s entire window is only 30 minutes (decision 8), so a daily cadence would risk recovering a genuinely-paid top-up up to 24 hours late. Expiry is driven by the attempt's own hard `expires_at` column directly, no separate `expire_after_hours` config needed (unlike membership's soft one).
- **Reseller-portal endpoints**, prefix `/api/reseller-portal` (a build-time pick, consistent with the task's own suggestion) — `App\Http\Controllers\ResellerPortal\{WalletController,OrderController,ProfileController,ApiKeyController}`, all behind `auth:affiliate` + `account.type:reseller`. `WalletController::show()`/`ApiKeyController::index()` reuse `ResellerWalletService`/`ResellerApiKeyService` as-is; `ApiKeyController::store()` enforces the 5-active-key cap (decision 7); `OrderController` is read-only (decision 2), explicitly filters `wallet_reseller_id` itself (no `BelongsToAffiliate`-style scope exists for it, and `affiliate.context` is deliberately not applied to this route group — a Reseller session has no meaning under ADR-057's Affiliate tenant scope).
- **`Admin\ResellerController::storeUser()`/`resendInvite()`** — decision 1's admin-triggered invite, added to the existing admin Reseller controller (not a new one), reusing `AffiliateInviteService` (generalized, see above) exactly as `Admin\AffiliateController`'s own staff-invite actions do. New `StoreResellerUserRequest`, new routes under `/admin/resellers/{reseller}/users*`.
- **`admin/` "Portal Users" row action, added same day** (the gap immediately below was caught before this PR was pushed — closed rather than left as a fast-follow): new `ResellerPortalUsersModal.tsx`, mirroring `AffiliateDetailModal.tsx`'s existing "Portal users" section (add-user form, invite-pending `Tag`, per-row "Resend invite") inside `ResellerApiKeysModal.tsx`'s own modal-per-row-action shape rather than a combined detail modal (this screen never had one — `/admin/resellers` opens `ResellerWalletModal`/`ResellerApiKeysModal`/`ResellerWhatsAppGroupsModal` per row already). `lib/resellers.ts` gained `getResellerDetail()` (the one fetch that eager-loads `users` — `listResellers()`'s row shape doesn't), `addResellerUser()`, `resendResellerUserInvite()`, all thin wrappers over `Admin\ResellerController`'s existing `storeUser()`/`resendInvite()`/`show()` — no backend change needed, it was already there. `npx tsc --noEmit`/`eslint`/`next build` clean on `admin/`; `ResellerControllerTest` (11/11) re-verified green, unaffected.
- **Reseller-portal frontend (`reseller/` app)** — `lib/auth.ts`'s `AffiliateSessionPayload` gained `owner_type`/`owner_id` (replacing `affiliate_id`, which no longer exists once the polymorphic migration landed); `login`/`impersonate` pages updated to read the new shape and to pick `business_name` from whichever of `affiliate`/`reseller` the login response actually populated. `PortalShell.tsx`'s nav branches on `session.owner_type` — `RESELLER_NAV` (Dashboard/Orders/Wallet/API Keys/Profile) vs. the existing `AFFILIATE_NAV` (unchanged, still 6 tabs + the impersonation banner). New `lib/reseller-portal.ts` (Wallet/Profile/API-key calls + the public payment-channel list) alongside the existing `lib/portal.ts` (now parameterized by `ownerType` for the shared Orders screen — `listOrders()`/`getOrder()` switch base path, the affiliate-only response fields — `reference_number`, `affiliate_profit`, customer/money detail — are typed optional and simply absent from the reseller-portal response, never present-but-zero). New pages `(portal)/wallet/page.tsx` (balance tile, top-up form redirecting to the CHIP checkout URL, ledger history) and `(portal)/api-keys/page.tsx` (issue/revoke, plaintext-once) — both built against this app's own existing `components/ui.tsx` read-screen primitives (`PageHeader`/`Panel`/`StatCard`/`StatusTag`/`ErrorNote`), not PrimeReact — this app never adopted PrimeReact for its own screens the way `admin/` did, so ADR-038's opportunistic-migration rule (which targets `admin/`'s hand-rolled TailAdmin primitives specifically) doesn't apply here. `profile/page.tsx` and `dashboard/page.tsx` both branch into a separate `Reseller*`/`Affiliate*` component per `owner_type`, rather than one component with scattered conditionals.
- **Build-time judgment call — no dedicated Reseller Dashboard backend endpoint.** The planning addendum's endpoint list (decision 2's "view + top-up + history only") never named a Reseller-specific dashboard summary. Rather than add a new backend endpoint for one screen, `(portal)/dashboard/page.tsx`'s `ResellerDashboard` composes the wallet balance (`GET /wallet`) and a 5-row recent-orders slice (`GET /orders?page=1`, already paginated) client-side.
- **Tests**: 55 new backend tests across `EnsureAccountTypeTest` (every existing Affiliate-only + new Reseller-only endpoint, both directions), `ResellerWalletTopupServiceTest`, `ResellerPortal\{Wallet,Order,Profile,ApiKey}ControllerTest`, `ChipWebhookControllerTest`'s new wallet-topup branch cases, `ReconcilePendingWalletTopupsCommandTest`, `ResellerControllerTest`'s new `storeUser`/`resendInvite` cases, plus the updated existing Affiliate-portal test files (`SetAffiliateContextTest` gained a reseller-owned-account rejection case; every `AffiliateUser::create()` call site across the suite updated `affiliate_id` → `owner_type`/`owner_id`). Full backend suite **1453/1453 fast** (sqlite, up from 1396) + **13/13 concurrency** (real MySQL, 1 new — `ResellerWalletTopupConcurrencyTest`, no regression on the existing 12), Pint clean on all 55 touched backend files. Migrated against the local dev DB (plain `migrate`, not `fresh`) — schema confirmed correct (`affiliate_users` has `owner_type`/`owner_id`, no `affiliate_id`; `wallet_topup_attempts` exists), zero rows to lose (local dev DB has no `affiliate_users` rows yet). `reseller/` app: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean, `npm run lint` clean, `npm run build` clean.
- **Note on the local test environment**: the sandboxed environment's `php artisan test` invocation silently caps its child PHPUnit process at PHP's compiled-in 128M default regardless of a `-d memory_limit=` flag on the outer command (the artisan wrapper shells out to a fresh process that doesn't inherit it) — every count above was produced by invoking `vendor/bin/phpunit`/`artisan test -c phpunit.concurrency.xml` directly with an explicit higher limit instead. Unrelated to this PR's own code (reproduces identically against `main` before this branch's changes) — noted here in case a future session hits the same "Fatal error: Allowed memory size exhausted" symptom running the full suite via the plain `composer test`/`php artisan test` invocation on this same machine.
- **Not done — explicitly deferred, same posture every prior PR's "not done" list has used**: the WhatsApp renewal-reminder half of a separate, unrelated backlog item is not this PR's concern; no self-serve signup (by design, decision 1); no platform-side maximum on the top-up amount (by design, decision 3 — `foundation-security.md` already carries this as an accepted risk).

No new grilling round needed — every branch opened this session resolved to a settled leaf in one pass. Code follows this addendum's shape exactly; a deviation found while building gets its own dated note here, same convention every other PR in this family already used.
